confirmed.title: Rituaali brand prefix `rit` baked into cookie and localStorage names of every product (kernel, generated client, committed openapi.json)
confirmed.evidence: openapi-config.ts:48 `.addCookieAuth("__Host-rit_session", ...)` and :53 "Nome configurável via COOKIE_NAME (default __Host-rit_session)"; packages/api-client/src/client.ts:65 `document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)rit_csrf=([^;]*)/)`; apps/web/src/shared/lib/last-location.ts:5 `const LAST_LOCATION_KEY = "rit-last-location"`; apps/web/src/shared/store/auth.store.ts:5 `const LOGOUT_CHANNEL_KEY = "rit-auth-logout"`; committed openapi.json:48 carries `__Host-rit_session` too.

Every client product's browser devtools will show `__Host-rit_session`, `rit_csrf`, `rit-last-location`, `rit-auth-logout` — an owner-brand leak into client runtime. Regenerate openapi.json and the contract snapshot.

confirmed.title: Catalog entry version '2.0.0' means two different codebases: tag v2.0.0 ships a pre-security-remediation 2.0.0, v2.1.0 a different 2.0.0
confirmed.evidence: git show v2.0.0:catalog/identity/single-tenant/module.json and v2.1.0:... both say "version": "2.0.0", yet `git diff v2.0.0 v2.1.0 -- catalog/` = 183 files changed, 5378 insertions(+), 927 deletions(-); at v2.0.0 the same manifest had "kernelRange": ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0", customMigrations ["01...","02_audit_attach.sql"] and no LOGIN_ACCOUNT_*/PASSWORD_HASH_MAX_IN_FLIGHT env; commit 2bd4da3 admits "v2.0.0 was cut before the merge" and a0f82a4 notes "entry-version residue". module add records only manifest.version in .platform-modules.lock (add.mjs:157) and clones the catalog at the child's template tag (_commit, catalog-source.mjs), so a v2.0.0 child installs the vulnerable code as "identity 2.0.0".
confirmed.why: The whole advisory/update machinery keys on module.json.version. Two products can hold identical lockfile versions with materially different (one insecure) code; `port-module-update` and `pnpm platform status` see nothing to do, and semver-range advisories cannot name the vulnerable population. This silently breaks the security-update promise of 'setup as a service'.
confirmed.recommendation: Never re-cut an already-tagged entry version: bump every entry touched by the remediation to 2.0.1/2.1.0 and record it in the CHANGELOGs (a follow-up tag v2.1.1 can carry only manifest bumps). Add a catalog-lint/CI rule that diffs each entry against its content at the last template tag and fails if files changed without a version bump. As a stopgap, make computePending also compare lock.catalogRef (already stored, add.mjs:160) so v2.0.0-ref children are treated as affected.
confirmed.original_title: Catalog entry version '2.0.0' means two different codebases: tag v2.0.0 ships a pre-security-remediation 2.0.0, v2.1.0 a different 2.0.0
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Reproduced: git show v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 both give identity "version": "2.0.0" with different kernelRange (>=1.0.0 <2.0.0 vs >=2.0.0 <3.0.0) and customMigrations, and `git diff v2.0.0 v2.1.0 -- catalog/` = 183 files, +5378/-927. All ten remediation advisories carry affects ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0", so computePending's semver.satisfies("2.0.0", ...) is false for a v2.0.0-generated child that installed the pre-remediation code as 2.0.0 — the advisory machinery reports nothing and `platform status` sees the module current. No later tag (through v2.2.1) bumps the entry versions; catalogRef is stored in the lock (add.mjs:160) but never consulted. Silently defeats the security-update promise.

confirmed.title: Identity entry ships the origin product's clinic/scheduling domain: professional areas/services, scheduling areas, default hours, serves_clients and birth_date are in the generic users schema and HTTP contract

confirmed.title: Every `pnpm platform` command crashes in the generated product: shipped catalog-graph.mjs imports the excluded lib/lint.mjs
confirmed.evidence: catalog-graph.mjs:4: `import { discoverEntries } from "./lint.mjs";` while copier.yml:46 excludes `scripts/platform/lib/lint.mjs`. Verified in a child rendered with `copier copy --trust --defaults --skip-tasks --vcs-ref HEAD`: `node scripts/platform/cli.mjs status` → `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../child/scripts/platform/lib/lint.mjs' imported from .../child/scripts/platform/lib/catalog-graph.mjs`. cli.mjs statically imports add.mjs → catalog-graph.mjs, so status/add/adopt/list all die at import time. The pair (import + exclusion) is present in tags v2.0.0, v2.1.0 and v2.2.0 (`git show v2.0.0:scripts/platform/lib/catalog-graph.mjs | grep lint` → same import; same _exclude line).
confirmed.why: The product's core value proposition — `pnpm platform module add`, `pnpm platform status` (the entry point of the template-update skill and of the session-start hook's advertised routine) — is dead on arrival in every product generated from the last three released tags. The child-manifest guard only checks package.json script strings, and template-smoke never executes the platform CLI in the child, so nothing catches it.
confirmed.recommendation: Move `discoverEntries` out of lint.mjs into a shipped module (e.g. into catalog-graph.mjs itself or a new lib/entries.mjs) or stop excluding lib/lint.mjs. Then close the guard gap: in template-smoke (or a node:test over the rendered child) run `node scripts/platform/cli.mjs status --offline` — or at minimum statically walk the import graph of every shipped scripts/** file and assert no edge lands on an _exclude'd path. Ship as a new tag + advisory since v2.0.0–v2.2.0 products are affected.

confirmed.why: Every client session in a fresh product (the normal state for 'setup as a service') gets a false instruction on SessionStart AND on the first prompt; an agent may obediently run `pnpm platform module adopt` on a product that has nothing to adopt, writing a bogus lock. It also fires in the template repo itself, where the lock will never exist. The test (pending-advisories.test.mjs 'sem .platform-modules.lock…') locks the wrong behaviour in.
confirmed.recommendation: Exit silently when there is no lock AND no vendored module to adopt (e.g. only emit the no-lock line when a module marker such as src/modules/* from the catalog is detected, or when the lock file exists but is empty of entries the product visibly has). At minimum special-case the template repo and the fresh product to silence.
confirmed.original_title: pending-advisories prints 'no .platform-modules.lock — run platform module adopt' in the template repo and in every freshly generated product with zero modules
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: copier.yml:54 excludes .platform-modules.lock from generation, readLock returns {modules:{}} for a missing file, computePending (advisories.mjs) returns noLock:true whenever modules is empty, and pending-advisories.mjs:31-33 then injects 'no .platform-modules.lock — run platform module adopt' on SessionStart and first prompt — i.e. in every freshly generated zero-module product (the deliverable's normal state) and in the template repo itself, instructing an action docs/dev/template.md:73 defines as a v0.2 migration only. False standing instruction in every client session; the test locks the behaviour in.

confirmed.title: Booking/hospitality domain leaks into agent tier guidance, verifier P0 definition and communication analogies
confirmed.evidence: subagent-model-required.mjs:42 'opus — only when the spec touches auth, payment, availability/booking rules, or data integrity (P0)'; spec-verifier.md:3 same list; tlc SKILL.md:80 example slug 'guest-agenda-full-load'; cards/orchestrator.md:90, sub-agents.md:59, validate.md:114, harness.md:129 repeat 'availability/booking rules'; communication.md:28,43 'guest, front desk, practitioner … front desk, guest record, cash drawer, room schedule, room key'.

A client in fintech/logistics/health gets 'booking rules' as their P0 category while their actual critical domain (ledger postings, prescriptions, inventory) is absent — so the Verifier under-escalates exactly where it matters. The analogies instruct agents to explain every reply in hotel terms.
confirmed.recommendation: Make the P0 list generic ('auth, payments, the product's core domain invariants — see docs/CONTEXT.md / product handbook — and data integrity') in the hook GUIDE, agent descriptions, cards and harness.md; make communication.md say 'analogies from the product's own business (see the product's domain glossary)'.
confirmed.original_title: Booking/hospitality domain leaks into agent tier guidance, verifier P0 definition and communication analogies

confirmed.title: feedback-triage.yml ships to every product but depends on a feedback module, endpoints and docs that don't exist

confirmed.title: Root .prettierrc points at nonexistent packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css — prettier crashes on every TS/TSX file in the template and in every generated product
confirmed.evidence: "plugins": ["prettier-plugin-tailwindcss"], "tailwindStylesheet": "packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css" — and `pnpm prettier --check apps/web/src/main.tsx` fails: "[error] apps/web/src/main.tsx: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css'". No `packages/ui` exists anywhere in the repo (see packages/ listing). .prettierrc is not in copier.yml `_exclude`, so every product receives it.
confirmed.why: `pnpm format`, `pnpm --filter web format`, `pnpm format:check` and editor format-on-save (prettier-vscode) are broken out of the box for every client. It is also residue of the owner's product (a packages/ui that only exists in RituaaliOS): both a robustness break and a template-hygiene leak. It escapes CI/gates only because format is not in `pnpm check` or lefthook.
confirmed.recommendation: Remove `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`, `tailwindStylesheet` and `tailwindFunctions` from the template's .prettierrc (the template ships no Tailwind — headless claim), and drop the root devDependency. Ship them as part of the UI-kit recipe/catalog entry instead. Add `pnpm format:check` to CI so a broken formatter can never ship again.
confirmed.original_title: Root .prettierrc points at nonexistent packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css — prettier crashes on every TS/TSX file in the template and in every generated product
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Reproduced: ./node_modules/.bin/prettier --check apps/web/src/main.tsx → ENOENT on packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css from prettier-plugin-tailwindcss loadV4; packages/ contains only api-client, eslint-config, typescript-config; .prettierrc is not excluded in copier.yml; .vscode/settings.json ships editor.formatOnSave:true with prettier as default formatter, so every save errors too. The template repo knows (.specs/STATE.md final bullet documents it as a follow-up 'left alone'), but .specs is copier-excluded so children inherit the breakage with no note, docs/code-quality.md:116/137 claims CI covers format, and the config is residue of the owner's packages/ui. High confirmed.

confirmed.title: Fresh product's Redis credentials are inconsistent: .env.example has no password, docker-compose requires one
confirmed.evidence: .env.example:49 `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379`; docker-compose.yml:34 `command: ["redis-server", "--requirepass", "redis"]` with comment :33 "Senha \"redis\" para casar com REDIS_URL=redis://:redis@localhost:6379 do .env"; docs/dev/local-environment.md:32 documents `redis://:redis@localhost:6379` as "already reflected in apps/api/.env".

confirmed.recommendation: Set `REDIS_URL=redis://:redis@localhost:6379` in apps/api/.env.example (matching compose), or drop `--requirepass` from the dev compose; align the local-environment.md table with whichever is chosen.
confirmed.original_title: Fresh product's Redis credentials are inconsistent: .env.example has no password, docker-compose requires one
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: README.md.jinja quickstart is literally 'cp apps/api/.env.example apps/api/.env' + 'docker compose up -d'; .env.example:49 has redis://localhost:6379 while docker-compose.yml:34 runs --requirepass redis (its own comment at :33 admits the example should carry the password) and local-environment.md:32 documents the passworded URL. confirmed.title: Fresh product's local loop is self-inconsistent: API port 3222 vs 3000 everywhere else, and compose Redis password absent from .env.example
confirmed.evidence: .env.example:5 `PORT=3222` and :49 `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379`; docker-compose.yml:34 starts Redis with `--requirepass redis` and its header comment claims 'Credenciais batem com apps/api/.env (... redis senha "redis")'; docs/dev/local-environment.md:32 documents `redis://:redis@localhost:6379`; apps/web/.env.example:2 `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000`; README.md.jinja:43 'API at http://localhost:3000'; docker-compose.yml:70 maps `3000:3000` for the api service while its env_file (.env from the example) sets PORT=3222, so the mapping reaches nothing.

confirmed.original_title: Fresh product's local loop is self-inconsistent: API port 3222 vs 3000 everywhere else, and compose Redis password absent from .env.example
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: All facts verified: PORT=3222 in .env.example and env.ts:14 default, apps/web/.env.example VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 (no vite proxy exists; apps/web/src/shared/config/env.test.ts even asserts 3000), README.md.jinja:43 says API at 3000, compose api publishes 3000:3000 while env_file carries PORT=3222. Fresh product: front cannot reach the api on the documented path, compose api's published port reaches nothing. confirmed.title: PORT is inconsistent across env schema (3222), Dockerfile (EXPOSE/healthcheck 3000) and compose (publishes 3000 while env_file sets 3222) — containerized API is unreachable or unhealthy unless PORT is manually overridden
confirmed.evidence: env.ts:14 `PORT: ...default(3222)` and .env.example:5 `PORT=3222`; Dockerfile:54 `EXPOSE 3000`, Dockerfile:57 healthcheck hits `process.env.PORT||3000`; docker-compose.yml api service: `env_file: apps/api/.env` (PORT=3222) + `ports: "3000:3000"` with no PORT override — the container listens on 3222 while compose publishes 3000. In prod, an image run without an explicit PORT listens on 3222 while the HEALTHCHECK probes 3000 → permanently unhealthy, restart loop under Swarm/K8s.
confirmed.why: The compose `api` service ('sobe tudo já migrado' convenience) is dead on arrival in every generated product, and the production image's healthcheck contradicts the application default — a real product deploying the image as-is gets killed by its own healthcheck.
confirmed.recommendation: Pick one port. Either default env PORT to 3000, or change Dockerfile EXPOSE/HEALTHCHECK fallback to 3222 and compose mapping to "3222:3222" (or set PORT explicitly in the compose service environment).
confirmed.original_title: PORT is inconsistent across env schema (3222), Dockerfile (EXPOSE/healthcheck 3000) and compose (publishes 3000 while env_file sets 3222) — containerized API is unreachable or unhealthy unless PORT is manually overridden
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: env.ts:14 defaults PORT to 3222; Dockerfile EXPOSE 3000 and HEALTHCHECK probes process.env.PORT||3000; compose api uses env_file apps/api/.env (PORT=3222 from the example, and the file is copier-excluded so compose even fails to start until it's created) with ports 3000:3000 and no PORT override. Containerized dev api is unreachable on its published port, and a prod image run without an explicit PORT listens on 3222 while the healthcheck probes 3000 — permanently unhealthy. Overlaps F-ci-docker-infra-6 but the prod-healthcheck consequence is its own distinct high.

confirmed.title: No raw-body/bootstrap seam in main.ts — payments/webhook signature verification (and the documented /docs-behind-login recipe) force editing a platform-owned file
confirmed.evidence: main.ts:35 `NestFactory.create(AppModule, { logger: ["error", "warn"] })` — no `rawBody: true`, no product hook; `rg "rawBody|express.raw"` over apps/api/src returns only problem-details.filter.ts. main.ts is not listed as product-owned in docs/dev/template.md's ownership table (composition root = app.module.ts, platform-modules.ts, schema.ts only). docs/dev/template.md's own recipe says "Replaces the current `/docs` mount" — which lives in main.ts/docs.ts.
confirmed.why: E-commerce/payments (Stripe/webhook HMAC needs the raw request body), CORS beyond one origin, custom body-size limits and middleware ordering all live in main.ts. The template's rule says products never edit platform files, yet these archetypes — and the template's own docs recipe — have no other place to go, making a copier conflict the designed path.
confirmed.recommendation: Enable `rawBody: true` in the factory (Nest only retains it for routes using RawBodyRequest) and add a product-owned `bootstrap.product.ts` (in `_skip_if_exists`, no-op default) that main.ts calls with `app` before listen — the extension point for docs guards, extra parsers, extra origins; explicitly list main.ts as platform in the ownership table.
confirmed.original_title: No raw-body/bootstrap seam in main.ts — payments/webhook signature verification (and the documented /docs-behind-login recipe) force editing a platform-owned file
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: NestFactory.create at main.ts:35 has no rawBody and no product hook; Nest installs its body parsers before any product MiddlewareConsumer middleware runs, so a Stripe-style webhook cannot reach the raw body without editing main.ts, which the ownership table (docs/dev/template.md:11-27) does not grant to the product; the template's own /docs-behind-login recipe (template.md:126) already instructs replacing a platform-owned mount, contradicting the conflict-free-update rule. Common product archetypes are forced into copier conflicts.

confirmed.title: API port story is inconsistent: env default 3222 vs README/web-env/Dockerfile 3000
confirmed.evidence: env.ts:14 `PORT: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(3222)`; apps/api/.env.example:5 `PORT=3222`; README.md.jinja:43 "API at `http://localhost:3000`"; apps/web/.env.example:2 `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000`; apps/api/Dockerfile:54 `EXPOSE 3000` and healthcheck `process.env.PORT||3000`; docker-compose.yml maps `3000:3000` for the api service while its env_file sets PORT=3222 (container listens on 3222, mapping and healthcheck point at 3000); docs/dev/local-environment.md:48 says "api (3222)".
confirmed.why: A fresh product's web front points at :3000 while the API boots on :3222 (host `pnpm dev` path), so the documented quickstart yields connection-refused; the compose `api` service is unhealthy/unreachable because the published port and healthcheck don't match the env-file port. Every client hits this on day one.
confirmed.recommendation: Pick one port (3000 is what Dockerfile/README/web assume): change the env.ts default and .env.example to 3000, or set VITE_API_URL/README/compose/healthcheck to 3222. Also override PORT=3000 explicitly in the compose api service either way.
confirmed.original_title: API port story is inconsistent: env default 3222 vs README/web-env/Dockerfile 3000
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: env.ts:14 defaults 3222, .env.example PORT=3222, README.md.jinja:43 and apps/web/.env.example say 3000, docker-compose maps 3000:3000 while env_file carries PORT=3222 (container listens on 3222, published port dead), Dockerfile EXPOSE 3000; the documented quickstart (cp .env.example .env; pnpm dev) yields a web front pointed at a port nothing listens on. One detail corrected: the healthcheck reads process.env.PORT so inside compose it probes the right port — the breakage is the port mapping, README and web env, which is still a day-one failure for every client.

confirmed.title: Coverage gate (pre-push + CI) is flaky: application-pool.int-spec's 150 ms connectionTimeoutMillis lets pg's connection-establishment timeout ('Connection terminated due to connection timeout') surface instead of the pool-wait timeout under load — fix the spec's margin; the untranslated second message is deliberate design, not a production 503 bug
confirmed.evidence:
Observed on a clean checkout, macOS + Docker 29.5.2: `pnpm test:coverage` run #1 → `Test Files  1 failed | 102 passed (103) / Tests  1 failed | 721 passed (722)`, `FAIL |api-int| src/shared/infra/database/application-pool.int-spec.ts > … > as duas formas de connect saem com PoolSaturatedError e o log traz o pool do instante` with `Error: Connection terminated due to connection timeout` (pg-pool/index.js:276). An isolated re-run of the same file failed identically; three later isolated runs and two later `test:coverage` runs passed (`Test Files 103 passed (103) / Tests 722 passed (722)`), i.e. 2 failures in 6 runs, both while the machine was busy.
Mechanism: `application-pool.int-spec.ts:303-312` builds the pool with `connectionTimeoutMillis: 150`, and `application-pool.ts:19` matches the pg error by exact string — `const ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE = "timeout exceeded when trying to connect"` — with `application-pool.ts:118` `if (error.message !== ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE) return error`. pg-pool's other timeout path emits `Connection terminated due to connection timeout`, which is therefore never wrapped in `PoolSaturatedError`.
confirmed.why: `test:coverage` is both the pre-push gate (`lefthook.yml`) and a CI job; a ~30 %-under-load failure means a freshly generated product blocks pushes and reds CI for reasons the client cannot diagnose. Worse, the same string-equality gap is a production defect: under a slow/loaded database the API answers 500 instead of the intended 503 + Retry-After.
confirmed.recommendation: Translate both pg timeout messages (or match `/timeout/` plus the pg-pool origin) in `translateAcquireError`, add a unit test for the second message, and raise `connectionTimeoutMillis` in the spec (e.g. 1000 ms) so the assertion does not depend on host latency.
confirmed.original_title: The coverage gate (pre-push + CI) is flaky: application-pool.int-spec fails ~1 run in 3 under load because the kernel translates only one of pg's two timeout errors
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: The flake mechanism and observations hold (application-pool.ts:19,118 exact-string match; spec builds the pool with connectionTimeoutMillis:150; failures observed 2/6 runs under load), and a flaky pre-push/CI gate in every product is high. But the 'production defect: 500 instead of 503' half is refuted: the spec's own comment ('o timeout de aquisição de verdade... falha de conexão real fica de fora') documents that real connection failures are deliberately not wrapped in PoolSaturatedError, and semantically a failed connection establishment is not pool saturation — so the fix belongs in the test margin, not in translating both messages.

confirmed.title: Storage is mandatory and hardwired to Cloudflare R2: boot fails without R2_* vars even for products that store nothing, and region 'auto' breaks genuine AWS S3
confirmed.evidence: app.module.ts:27 imports StorageModule unconditionally; storage.module.ts:12 `useFactory: () => new R2StorageAdapter(loadStorageConfig())` — storage.config.ts requires R2_ACCOUNT_ID/R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/R2_BUCKET/R2_ENDPOINT (fail-fast Zod). r2-storage.adapter.ts:36 `region: "auto"` with comment 'o exigido pelo R2'; no region env exists. .env.example ships `R2_ACCOUNT_ID=changeme` etc.
confirmed.why: A kernel-only product with zero modules cannot boot without inventing fake R2 credentials; a product on AWS S3 gets SigV4 signature failures (region 'auto' is R2-specific), and MinIO/GCS/local-disk products must edit platform-owned files (storage.config.ts / r2-storage.adapter.ts / storage.module.ts), breaking the 'product adds, never edits' copier-update contract. Env var names themselves (R2_*) are provider-branded.
confirmed.recommendation: Rename vars to provider-neutral STORAGE_* with STORAGE_REGION (default 'auto'), make the module lazy/optional (e.g. NullStorageAdapter that throws StorageUnavailable on use when unconfigured, or validate config only on first injection), keeping ObjectStoragePort as the seam.
confirmed.original_title: Storage is mandatory and hardwired to Cloudflare R2: boot fails without R2_* vars even for products that store nothing, and region 'auto' breaks genuine AWS S3
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: app.module.ts imports StorageModule unconditionally; storage.module.ts useFactory eagerly calls loadStorageConfig() (Zod fail-fast on R2_ACCOUNT_ID/R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/R2_BUCKET/R2_ENDPOINT); r2-storage.adapter.ts:36 pins region 'auto' (R2-only, breaks AWS SigV4) with no region env. The template's own CI proves the cost: .github/workflows/catalog.yml has to export five placeholder R2_* vars just to boot. No health-check involvement, so boot with fake creds works — but any S3/MinIO/GCS product must edit platform-owned files, breaking the copier-update contract.

confirmed.title: store.tenantId has no sanctioned HTTP writer: readonly, initialized null, setActor never copies actor.tenantId — multi-tenant products silently record null everywhere unless they discover an undocumented nested ctx.run() workaround
confirmed.evidence: request-context.ts:30 `readonly tenantId: string | null` (only `actor` and `extensions` are writable; `setActor` writes only actor); request-context.middleware.ts:49 creates the HTTP store with `tenantId: null`. Consumers read it anyway: outbox.publisher.ts:42 `tenantId: ctx.tenantId`, idempotency.interceptor.ts:113 `const scope = `${ctx?.tenantId ?? "_"}:${principal}``, logger.factory.ts:53. docs/arch/back.md:191 claims "RequestContext provides the actor, correlationId and tenantId". The identity middleware itself reads it (`const { tenantId } = this.ctx.get()`) — always null. The catalog ships only `identity/single-tenant`.
confirmed.why: Multi-tenant B2B SaaS is the single most common setup-service archetype. The kernel models tenantId in the outbox envelope, idempotency scope, event/job contexts and logs, but there is no writer for HTTP ingress: a tenancy module cannot populate it without editing the kernel (a designed copier conflict). Every tenant column stays null; idempotency keys collapse to `_:actorId`; events carry no tenant.
confirmed.recommendation: Add a one-shot `setTenant(tenantId: string)` symmetric to `setActor` (null→value, second call throws), called by the tenancy/identity middleware; alternatively have `setActor` copy `actor.tenantId` into the store. Then ship (or at least spec) an `identity/multi-tenant` variant that resolves tenant from host/header and calls it.
confirmed.original_title: Multi-tenant seam is a dead end: store.tenantId is readonly-null over HTTP and nothing can ever set it
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Facts verified: request-context.ts:30 readonly tenantId; middleware sets null; setActor (lines 57-63) writes only store.actor even though Actor carries optional tenantId; consumers (outbox.publisher.ts:42, idempotency.interceptor.ts:113, logger.factory.ts:53, identity auth.middleware.ts:155) all read the always-null field, and back.md rule 24 claims RequestContext 'provides tenantId'. Strictly, 'nothing can ever set it' is refutable: a product middleware can call the public RequestContext.run({...ctx.get(), tenantId}, next) — AsyncLocalStorage nests — without editing the kernel. But that path is undocumented, order-fragile, and no doc or module hints at it, so a real multi-tenant product ships null tenant columns, collapsed idempotency scopes and tenant-less events before finding it. High stands.

confirmed.title: The kernel test harness shipped to every product hardcodes catalog-module schemas and the owner's brand cookie names — and RULE C's scan is scoped so it cannot see them
confirmed.evidence:
`apps/api/test/setup/test-db.ts:98-124` (copied into every product; not excluded in `copier.yml`) exports `truncateIdentity` with `TRUNCATE TABLE identity.auth_events, identity.verification_tokens, identity.permission_templates, identity.sessions, identity.professional_default_hours, identity.users`, plus `truncateAttachment` (`attachment.*`) and `truncateTag` (`tag.tags`) — schemas that only exist once the matching catalog entry is installed, and `professional_default_hours` is a business-domain table of the owner's own product.
`apps/api/test/setup/unit-env.ts:23-24` and `e2e-env.ts:25-26` set `process.env.COOKIE_NAME = "rit_session"` / `DEVICE_COOKIE_NAME = "rit_device"` (plus `PASSWORD_PEPPER`, `CSRF_SECRET`, `BREACH_CHECK_*`) — none of these keys exist in the kernel's `apps/api/src/shared/config/env.ts` schema; they belong to the identity entry, and `rit_` is the owner's brand.
RULE C cannot catch this: `apps/api/src/modules/module-boundaries.spec.ts:539-545` scans only `SHARED_DIR`, `app.module.ts`, `db/schema.ts`, `web/src/app`, `web/src/shared` — `apps/api/test/**`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `src/openapi`, `src/docs` are outside the surface. The coupling is real, not vestigial: `catalog/identity/single-tenant/api/__e2e__/*.e2e-spec.ts:6` imports `truncateIdentity` from `../../../../test/setup/test-db`.
confirmed.why: CLAUDE.md's first rule is "nothing product-specific enters" and the spec's own comment claims "nenhum token de identity/attachment/audit/notification/tag sobrevive na casca do template". Every client repo therefore ships SQL for schemas they may never install and a cookie name from another company's product, while the guard that is supposed to prevent exactly this reports green.
confirmed.recommendation: Move the per-module truncate helpers and module env defaults out of the kernel harness into each catalog entry (e.g. `catalog/<entry>/api/testing/truncate.ts`, installed with the entry), keep only `truncateKernel` in `test-db.ts`, and extend `KERNEL_SURFACE` to `apps/api/test`, `apps/api/src/openapi`, `apps/api/src/docs` and `apps/web/src/pages` so RULE C actually covers the shipped shell.
confirmed.original_title: The kernel test harness shipped to every product hardcodes catalog-module schemas and the owner's brand cookie names — and RULE C's scan is scoped so it cannot see them

confirmed.title: `pnpm install` and `skills:sync` tasks run three times per `copier update` — twice in throwaway temp renders
confirmed.evidence: Verified empirically with copier 9.17.2: a task logging `$PWD` during `copier update` ran with `op=update` in `copier._main.old_copy.*`, in the real project, and in `copier._main.new_copy.*` (copier's _apply_update calls run_copy — which executes _tasks — for both temporary renders; only `git init` is skipped via its `_copier_operation == 'copy'` guard). copier.yml:70 `- command: pnpm install` and :72 `pnpm skills:sync` carry only the `not _copier_conf.pretend` condition.
confirmed.why: Each `copier update` performs two full monorepo installs in temp dirs that are immediately deleted (minutes + network each; offline or registry hiccup aborts the whole update mid-flight), plus one in the real project that runs BEFORE the product's diff is reapplied — so it installs against the pristine template manifest and the final node_modules/lockfile are stale anyway (the template-update skill already re-runs `pnpm install` after the merge). Pure cost and a new failure mode, zero benefit.
confirmed.recommendation: Gate both with `when: "{{ _copier_operation == 'copy' and not _copier_conf.pretend }}"` (like git init). Keep the package.json prune task unconditional — it must run in old/new temp copies so the 3-way diff stays consistent with the pruned product manifest.

confirmed.title: ADV-20260822-01..05 affects '>=1.0.0 <2.0.0' excludes the vulnerable entry version 2.0.0 shipped at tag v2.0.0 — pending-advisories silently reports those children clean, and the documented 'apply by hand' fallback is defeated by the same range

Add a lint rule: an advisory's affects range must exclude only versions whose content actually contains the fix.

confirmed.title: pt-BR is hardcoded as the product language across shipped docs rules, agent-reply mandate, issue conventions, web html lang/Zod messages and three kernel locale fallbacks, with no copier locale question and no single swap point — a non-Brazilian client's product works but requires a manual multi-file sweep to change language

confirmed.title: Native Windows is not a viable client platform, but the template never says so — the only OS mention implies it works
confirmed.evidence: docs/dev/local-environment.md:9 "- Docker Desktop (with WSL2 enabled on Windows)." — the sole OS statement in the shipped docs (grep for windows|wsl|macos|linux across README.md.jinja, TEMPLATE.md, docs/dev/*.md, AGENTS.md.jinja returns only this line). confirmed.why: CONSOLIDATED VERDICT for this probe: on native Windows, product generation self-destructs (see the ln finding), `copier update` fails, all 11 agent skills silently vanish on clone, and the hook/gate harness either errors on every event or silently no-ops. Under WSL2 everything works (POSIX shell, real symlinks, ps/lsof). So the honest support matrix today is macOS / Linux / WSL2 — but a client reading local-environment.md's "Docker Desktop (with WSL2 enabled on Windows)" will reasonably conclude native Windows development is supported, and a setup-as-a-service seller cannot afford that discovery to happen at the client. Note .gitattributes already handles EOL correctly (`* text=auto eol=lf`), so line endings are NOT the problem — symlinks, `ln`, `$VAR` expansion and '/'-only path regexes are.

Native Windows is not supported." — in README.md.jinja's prerequisites, docs/dev/local-environment.md (replacing/extending line 9), TEMPLATE.md, and ideally copier.yml's `_message_after_copy`. If Windows-native clients matter commercially, instead apply the specific fixes in the other findings (regular-file CLAUDE.md, junction/copy fallback in skills:sync, relative hook paths, path.sep-normalized gates).

confirmed.title: CSRF double-submit is unimplementable in the very topology it targets: rit_csrf is a host-only cookie on the API host, but the SPA reads document.cookie on the front origin
confirmed.evidence: client.ts:63-67 reads `document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)rit_csrf=/)` in the SPA. catalog/identity/.../api/guards/cookie.ts:90-95 sets rit_csrf with `path: "/"` and NO `domain` attribute (host-only on the API host), and csrf.guard.ts enforces `assertDoubleSubmit` on every authenticated mutation when `COOKIE_SAMESITE === "none"`. copier.yml defaults front to `<app_domain>` and API to `api.<app_domain>` — different hosts.
confirmed.why: SameSite=None is the cross-host/cross-site configuration, yet a cookie set by api.<app_domain> is never visible to document.cookie on <app_domain>: readCsrfToken() always returns null, the X-CSRF-Token header is never sent, and every authenticated mutation gets 403 from CsrfGuard. The e2e test (auth-csrf-none.e2e-spec.ts) passes only because supertest reads Set-Cookie directly, which a browser SPA cannot do. Additionally Safari/Chrome third-party-cookie policies make the None+cross-site session cookie itself unreliable. Any client product that flips COOKIE_SAMESITE=none is bricked at runtime.
confirmed.recommendation: Deliver the CSRF token through a channel the front can read cross-origin: echo it in the login/GET /auth/session response body (or a response header) and have configureClient store it in memory; or document loudly that SameSite=None requires serving the API under the front's own origin (reverse-proxy path), and make identity.config refuse None when WEB_ORIGIN's host differs from the API host.
confirmed.original_title: CSRF double-submit is unimplementable in the very topology it targets: rit_csrf is a host-only cookie on the API host, but the SPA reads document.cookie on the front origin
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified end-to-end: cookie.ts:85-99 sets rit_csrf host-only (no domain) on the API host; no controller exposes the token any other way (all setCsrfCookie call sites checked — login, set-password, confirm-email-change, get-session, cookie only); csrf.guard.ts:62-64 requires the double-submit header on every authenticated mutation when COOKIE_SAMESITE=none; client.ts:63-67 can only read document.cookie on the front origin. In the cross-site topology that is the only reason to set none, the SPA can never send X-CSRF-Token and every authenticated mutation 403s. Default lax works (subdomains are same-site), so it is a latent brick for any product flipping the documented switch (module.json: 'none liga o double-submit') — high, not critical.

confirmed.title: "CI fails on an uncommitted openapi.json" is promised to every client but no gate regenerates or diffs the contract
confirmed.evidence:
`README.md.jinja:23` (copied into every product): "Zod → DTOs → `openapi.json` → generated client (`@platform/api-client`); CI fails on an uncommitted contract"; same claim in `docs/arch/back.md:78` ("CI fails on an uncommitted `openapi.json`") and `.github/README.md:38`.
Grep over `.github/workflows/*` finds no `pnpm contract` / `contract-diff` / `git diff --exit-code` step; `ci.yml` jobs are `quality`, `test-unit`, `test-coverage` only.
The only "contract" test is `apps/api/test/openapi-contract.e2e-spec.ts:17`, which re-reads the *committed* file (`resolve(__dirname, "../../../openapi.json")`) and snapshots it — it can never detect that the file is stale relative to the code, and `scripts/platform/lib/apply.mjs:17-21` (`TEMPLATE_ONLY_FILES`) deletes both it and its snapshot on the first `pnpm platform module add`.

confirmed.recommendation: Add a CI step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (product-visible workflow) that runs `pnpm contract` and then `git diff --exit-code openapi.json packages/api-client/generated`, and keep a version of that check alive after the first `module add` (it must not be in `TEMPLATE_ONLY_FILES`). confirmed.title: .platform-modules.lock records absolute machine paths for every copied file (and local catalogRef), breaking portability, rollback on other checkouts, and the port-module-update hash gate
confirmed.evidence: planCopy builds `to = path.join(targetRoot=cwd, ...)` and add.mjs stores `files: files.map((file) => file.to)`; writeLock (apply.mjs:144) persists them verbatim. Real install produced `"path": "/private/tmp/.../with space/child/apps/api/src/modules/alpha/alpha.module.ts"` and `"catalogRef": "/Users/emanuelvogt/.../fixtures/catalog"` in the committed lock. .agents/skills/port-module-update/SKILL.md:43 documents and depends on child-relative paths (`"path": "apps/api/src/modules/notification/..."`).
confirmed.why: The lock is committed ('never edited by hand'): it leaks the generating developer's filesystem layout to the whole client team; a teammate's `--rollback` matches nothing (existsSync on the other machine's absolute path) and silently removes only the lock entry; the port-module-update skill's sha256 gate maps catalog paths to relative install paths and will never match the lock's absolute keys — hash verification on update is effectively dead.
confirmed.recommendation: Store paths relative to the child root (path.relative(cwd, to)) in the lock and resolve against cwd on read; write catalogRef only for git sources or normalize local ones. Add a lock-shape test asserting no absolute path is persisted.
confirmed.original_title: .platform-modules.lock records absolute machine paths for every copied file (and local catalogRef), breaking portability, rollback on other checkouts, and the port-module-update hash gate
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: planCopy builds `to` via childLayout(targetRoot=cwd) with absolute joins (child-layout.mjs:26-38, plan.mjs:91), add.mjs:161 stores `files.map(f=>f.to)`, apply.mjs:144 persists them verbatim and lock.mjs does no normalization; the lock is not gitignored and copier lists it in _skip_if_exists, so it is a committed file. rollback (apply.mjs:158-159) existsSync's the absolute path, so on any other checkout it deletes nothing; port-module-update SKILL.md:43 documents child-relative paths, so its sha256 gate can never match absolute keys.

confirmed.title: Product generated off-tag (`--vcs-ref HEAD` or any commit past a tag) can never `module add`: describe-style `_commit` fails both kernelRange and git clone
confirmed.evidence: add.mjs:40 `answers._commit ? String(answers._commit).replace(/^v/, "") : undefined` feeds semver.satisfies directly. Verified: `semver.satisfies("2.1.0-3-gabc1234", ">=2.0.0") === false` (prerelease semantics) -> exit 8 KERNEL_RANGE_UNSATISFIED for every entry. Also catalog-source.mjs:81-94 runs `git clone --branch <gitRef>` with gitRef = `_commit`; verified `git clone --depth 1 ... --branch v2.1.0-3-gab7685f` fails ("Remote branch not found"), same for a bare SHA -> exit 3. The template repo itself is at `git describe` = v2.1.0-4-gb266210 right now, and .github/README.md:160 documents `--vcs-ref HEAD` as a supported generation mode. A `_commit`-less answers file (local dir source) yields templateVersion undefined -> exit 8 with the message "template está em undefined".
confirmed.why: Any client product generated from a commit that is not exactly a v-tag (including one generated today from main) is permanently locked out of the module catalog with misleading errors. template-version.mjs already has parseInstalledVersion() that handles the describe format correctly, but add.mjs does not use it.
confirmed.recommendation: In readTemplateVersion, parse `_commit` with parseInstalledVersion() and use the base tag (a repo N commits past v2.1.0 has kernel 2.1.0). In resolveCatalog, split a describe ref into tag + sha: clone the tag, or clone default branch and `git fetch origin <sha> && git checkout` for SHAs. Cover both in tests (no test today exercises addCommand with a describe-style or missing `_commit`).
confirmed.original_title: Product generated off-tag (`--vcs-ref HEAD` or any commit past a tag) can never `module add`: describe-style `_commit` fails both kernelRange and git clone
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Both halves verified at HEAD: add.mjs:36-40 feeds raw _commit into semver.satisfies and I confirmed semver.valid('2.1.0-3-gabc1234') is truthy yet satisfies('...','>=2.0.0')===false (prerelease semantics), and satisfies(undefined,...)===false → exit 8 with 'template está em undefined'; catalog-source.mjs still clones with --branch <describe-string>, which git rejects. parseInstalledVersion (template-version.mjs:32-37) handles the format correctly but add.mjs does not use it; all five entries declare kernelRange '>=2.0.0 <3.0.0'. Any product generated off-tag (--vcs-ref HEAD is documented in .github/README.md:160) is locked out of the catalog. confirmed.title: `--rollback` with an unreachable catalog silently wipes the registry of ALL other installed modules
confirmed.evidence: runRollback: `try { ... entries = buildRegistryEntries(...) } catch { entries = []; }` (add.mjs:71-77) then writeRegistry unconditionally. Reproduced: installed alpha+beta, ran `module add beta --rollback --catalog-ref /nope` -> exit 0, 'beta revertido', and apps/api/src/platform-modules.ts went from importing AlphaModule+BetaModule to `export const PLATFORM_MODULES = [] as const;` while alpha is still in the lock and its files still on disk.
confirmed.why: Rollback is exactly the command a user reaches for when something is already broken (often offline or with a bad ref); it then desyncs lock vs registry for unrelated modules, silently unmounting them from the Nest app. Exit code is 0, so nothing signals the damage.
confirmed.recommendation: If the catalog is unreachable during rollback, rebuild the registry from information already in the lock (store apiModule/schemaExports per entry in the lock at install time so the catalog is not needed), or abort the registry rewrite with a warning and non-zero exit instead of writing an empty registry.

Reporter's reproduction matches the code path exactly; no test or guard covers rollback with an unreachable catalog.

confirmed.title: --rollback reverts only the target module of a failed --with-deps add: deps stay installed with no contract regen (pnpm check red), and the batch has no tool-assisted unwind — though the probe's root-cause migration corruption is fixed at HEAD (90f1d0d) and template-only removal is documented deliberate

confirmed.title: `advisory detect` is unreliable in every shipped advisory: rg convention inverted, quotes passed literally, `;` chains unsupported, missing binary reports 'não afetado'
confirmed.evidence: advisory.mjs:20-22: `advisory.detect.split(" ")` then `affected = result.status === 1`. All 10 shipped advisories use `detect: "rg -l 'jest\\.' apps/..."` style. (a) split-on-space passes the argv `['-l', "'jest\\.'", path]` — the single quotes become part of the regex (verified argv), so the pattern never matches; (b) rg exits 0 on match / 1 on no match, so even with correct quoting an affected child (jest present) exits 0 = 'não afetado' and a migrated child exits 1 = 'afetado' — inverted against docs/advisories/README.md's 'exit 1 = child affected'; (c) ADV-20260822-04's detect chains two commands with `;`, impossible without a shell; (d) verified spawnSync ENOENT gives status null, and defaultRun (`result.status ?? 0`) maps it to 0 -> 'não afetado' — ripgrep is not a dependency of the product, so on a machine without rg every advisory reports not affected.
confirmed.why: The advisory channel is the security/bugfix distribution mechanism of the whole offering; as shipped it reports the exact opposite of reality or a silent all-clear depending on whether rg is installed. cli.test.mjs only tests detect with a stubbed run, so none of this is caught.
confirmed.recommendation: Run detect through a shell (`spawnSync(cmd, {shell: true})`) so quoting and `;` work; define and enforce the exit convention in one place (either flip to 'exit 0 = affected, 1 = clean' matching grep/rg semantics and fix README, or wrap rg-based detects in `! rg ...`); treat status null/ENOENT and status >=2 as a distinct 'detect failed' exit code, never as 'not affected'; also note detect exit 1 currently collides with EXIT_CODES.ADVISORY_INVALID=1 (advisory not found is indistinguishable from affected). Add tests against the real advisory files' detect strings.
confirmed.original_title: `advisory detect` is unreliable in every shipped advisory: rg convention inverted, quotes passed literally, `;` chains unsupported, missing binary reports 'não afetado'
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Fully reproduced: advisory.mjs:20 argv split keeps the quotes (["rg","-l","'jest\\.'",...]); spawnSync on a missing binary returns status null and defaultRun's 'status ?? 0' coalesces it to 'não afetado' (rg is not a product dependency); rg exit convention is inverted vs README; ';' chains are unexecutable; detect exit 1 collides with EXIT_CODES.ADVISORY_INVALID=1; cli.test.mjs only exercises a stubbed one-token 'meu-detector'. The advisory channel — the security-fix distribution mechanism of the offering — gives systematically wrong answers in every shipped advisory. Canonical finding for the detect cluster.

confirmed.title: branch-only-in-worktree blocks commands that merely mention 'git checkout -b' inside quoted strings or heredocs
confirmed.evidence: Probe: echo "use git checkout -b foo in the worktree" → exit 2 'Branch creation blocked in the main checkout'. It also blocked this audit's own live Bash call, which only contained the string inside a heredoc being written to a file.
confirmed.why: The tokenizer splits on whitespace with no quote awareness, so writing docs, tests, or scripts that mention branch commands via Bash (heredoc, echo, git commit messages spanning segments) is falsely blocked with exit 2 — a hard block the agent must hack around, in any client product.
confirmed.recommendation: Strip quoted substrings and heredoc bodies before tokenizing, or only classify a segment when its first non-env token is git (as the delegate hook's head() does).
confirmed.original_title: branch-only-in-worktree blocks commands that merely mention 'git checkout -b' inside quoted strings or heredocs

Cause verified in code: line ~81 splits segments on &&/||/;/|/newline and tokenizes on whitespace with zero quote/heredoc awareness, then createsBranch matches any -b after a 'git' token anywhere in the segment — so echo/printf/commit-message/heredoc mentions of branch commands are hard-blocked (exit 2) in the main checkout of every client product.

confirmed.why: touchesDocs and the write-detectors are matched independently over the whole command string, so reading a doc into a pipe, copying a doc OUT of docs/, or editing source while a docs path appears anywhere in the text is falsely hard-blocked. Agents in every product hit this whenever a command references a handbook.
confirmed.recommendation: Analyse per statement and verify the write TARGET is the docs path (redirect destination, tee argument, cp/mv destination, sed -i operand), not just co-occurrence in the string.
confirmed.original_title: docs-stay-lean's Bash gate blocks any command whose text contains a docs path plus tee/sed -i/cp anywhere, regardless of what is actually written
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: docs-stay-lean.mjs:55-64: touchesDocs and each write-detector are matched independently over the whole command string — /\btee\b/ and sed -i anywhere trigger with any docs path mention anywhere (even inside a quoted string preceded by ', which satisfies the (^|[\s"'=(]) prefix), and the cp/mv regex matches when the doc is the SOURCE (`cp docs/x.md /tmp/`). All probe behaviours reproduce from the regexes; false hard-blocks (exit 2) whenever a compound command references a handbook.

confirmed.title: docs-stay-lean's rationale gate is pt-BR/Spanish-specific and applies to every docs/**/*.md a client writes, while English rationale passes
confirmed.evidence: Probes on docs/product/guide.md: 'We chose X because Y.' → pass; 'Escolhemos X porque Y.' → blocked; 'Hay un problema porque el servidor.' (Spanish) → blocked; 'A justificativa fiscal exige NF-e' (domain term) → blocked; 'See the trade-off table.' → blocked; '## Context' → blocked; new 100-line docs/product/onboarding.md → blocked (cap 80)
confirmed.why: For a product-agnostic template the enforcement is asymmetric by language (a Portuguese or Spanish team is blocked on ordinary words; an English team is not) and over-broad in scope: the growth/rationale caps hit product/business docs the client legitimately owns, not just the platform handbooks the rule was written for.
confirmed.recommendation: Scope HANDBOOK to the known platform handbook paths (docs/arch, docs/agents, docs/test, docs/code-quality.md, CLAUDE/AGENTS) instead of all of docs/, and either make the phrase list locale-neutral (headings only) or configurable via a copier answer.
confirmed.original_title: docs-stay-lean's rationale gate is pt-BR/Spanish-specific and applies to every docs/**/*.md a client writes, while English rationale passes
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: RATIONALE_PHRASE (docs-stay-lean.mjs:30-31) lists Portuguese rationale words (porque, optamos, decidimos, justificativa — 'porque' also Spanish) plus only 'trade-offs?' in English, so 'because'/'we chose' pass while ordinary pt/es prose is blocked; HANDBOOK (line 23) covers ALL docs/**/*.md except adr/ and advisories/, so a client's own product docs (docs/product/*) inherit the 80-line new-file cap, 30-line growth cap and the pt-BR-centric phrase gate. Asymmetric by language and over-broad in scope for a product-agnostic template.

confirmed.title: kill-orphan-dev-servers on Linux never kills detached main-repo orphans (tty '?' vs macOS '??'); linked-worktree cleanup still works
confirmed.evidence: `const detached = tty === "??"` — BSD/macOS ps prints '??' for no controlling terminal; procps (Linux) prints '?'. A detached orphan on Linux is classified non-detached, then skipped unless in a linked worktree.
confirmed.why: Products deploy to teams on Linux; the SessionEnd cleanup silently never fires there, leaving orphan dev servers holding ports — the exact problem the hook exists to solve, invisible because the hook exits 0.
confirmed.original_title: kill-orphan-dev-servers is inert on Linux: detached test hardcodes macOS's '??' tty; Linux ps prints '?'
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Line 73 `const detached = tty === "??"` misses procps's single '?', so a detached orphan in the main repo fails line 74's `!detached && !isLinkedWorktree` check and is skipped on Linux — but a vite process in a linked worktree passes isLinkedWorktree regardless of tty and is still killed, so 'inert on Linux' overstates it. The main-repo orphan case (the hook's headline scenario, small features run in the main repo) silently never fires on Linux; one-character fix.

confirmed.title: Session-start hook injects a false 'run platform module adopt' nudge in every fresh product and in the template repo itself
confirmed.evidence: With no .platform-modules.lock (the state of every freshly generated kernel-only product, and of the template repo): `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"no .platform-modules.lock — run platform module adopt"}}` — reproduced with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at the fresh child and at /Users/emanuelvogt/Developer/platform-template.
confirmed.why: A kernel-only product with zero modules has nothing to adopt, yet every session begins by steering the agent toward `pnpm platform module adopt` — a command that today crashes outright (finding #1). In the template repo the advice is meaningless. False positives at session start erode trust in the harness's real warnings.
confirmed.recommendation: Emit the no-lock line only when module files are actually present without a lock (e.g. apps/api/src/modules contains more than module-boundaries.spec.ts), and skip entirely when cwd is the template repo (no .copier-answers.yml).
confirmed.original_title: Session-start hook injects a false 'run platform module adopt' nudge in every fresh product and in the template repo itself
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: computePending (scripts/platform/lib/advisories.mjs) returns noLock:true whenever lock.modules is empty, and the hook maps that to 'no .platform-modules.lock — run platform module adopt'. The template ships no .platform-modules.lock (it is only in _skip_if_exists, copier.yml:54), so every fresh kernel-only product and the template repo itself get the nudge at every SessionStart/first prompt despite having nothing to adopt.

confirmed.title: specs-in-english blocks English prose that quotes pt-BR product strings — contradicting its own header claim
confirmed.evidence: Header: 'Quoted product strings ("Sem horário") inside English prose stay under the threshold by construction'. Probe: an English sentence listing quoted UI labels ('Não há horário', 'Sem vagas', …) → blocked: 'reads as pt-BR prose (11 pt-BR function words in 25...)'. Only backticks/code fences/URLs are stripped, not '…'/"…" quotes.
confirmed.why: The owner's own market is pt-BR products: any spec that enumerates a screen's UI labels in normal quotes is hard-blocked, and the error text tells the agent that quoting product strings is the sanctioned way — a loop. Also: the gate only detects pt-BR, so a Spanish client's non-English specs pass silently ('El usuario no puede crear una reserva…' → exit 0) although the rule says .specs is English-only.
confirmed.recommendation: Strip single/double-quoted spans before counting words (matching the documented contract), and document that detection is pt-BR-only or add per-locale stopword lists.
confirmed.original_title: specs-in-english blocks English prose that quotes pt-BR product strings — contradicting its own header claim
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Reproduced both probes: an English sentence quoting five pt-BR UI labels in double quotes is blocked (exit 2, '7 pt-BR function words in 25'), directly contradicting the header claim at specs-in-english.mjs:8-9 that quoted product strings stay under the threshold; the error text tells the agent quoting is the sanctioned path (loop, though backtick-quoting escapes since inline code is stripped). Spanish prose passes with exit 0, so the English-only rule is enforced only against pt-BR.

confirmed.title: pending-advisories and template-behind crash with an ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND stack trace when node_modules is absent, despite headers claiming 'any failure exits silently'
confirmed.evidence: Running both hooks in a product-shaped dir without node_modules: "Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'yaml' imported from .../scripts/platform/lib/template-version.mjs" exit=1 (same for 'semver' via advisories.mjs). The try/catch inside the hook cannot catch top-level static import failures.
confirmed.why: A client clones their generated repo and opens Claude Code before running pnpm install (or in a CI checkout): every SessionStart and first prompt dumps a Node stack trace as a hook warning. Non-blocking (exit 1, not 2) but noisy and looks broken — exactly the first impression a setup-as-a-service template must not give.
confirmed.recommendation: Move the imports to dynamic `await import()` inside the try block, or drop the yaml/semver deps for these two call-sites (the _src_path/_commit lines and the semver-range check are trivially parseable by hand), or exit 0 early when <projectDir>/node_modules is missing.
confirmed.original_title: pending-advisories and template-behind crash with an ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND stack trace when node_modules is absent, despite headers claiming 'any failure exits silently'
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Reproduced in a product-shaped copy without node_modules: pending-advisories.mjs dies with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND ('semver' via advisories.mjs) exit 1 and a full stack trace; template-behind.mjs has the same shape via template-version.mjs's static `import { parse } from 'yaml'`. Static imports are hoisted, so the in-body try/catch that promises 'any failure exits silently' cannot catch them. Hits any clone opened before pnpm install; non-blocking but noisy.

confirmed.title: Generated products commit their .claude/skills symlinks (skills:sync runs before the first commit, .gitignore does not cover them) — a Windows teammate's clone silently loads zero skills
confirmed.evidence: `git ls-files -s | awk '$1==120000'` → 11 symlinks under .claude/skills (blob content e.g. `../../.agents/skills/grilling`). copier.yml excludes `.claude/skills` from the copy, but the `pnpm skills:sync` task (copier.yml:72) recreates the symlinks after `git init` (copier.yml:66) and before the client's first commit; .gitignore does not ignore .claude/skills (git check-ignore returns nothing), so the product commits them exactly like the template does.
confirmed.why: Git for Windows defaults to core.symlinks=false (real symlinks need Developer Mode AND opting in at install), so a Windows teammate on any client team clones the product and gets 11 one-line text files where skill directories should be. Claude Code finds no SKILL.md and loads zero skills — no error, no warning: the sold harness feature (catalog-modules, template-update via its .claude mirror, tlc-spec-driven, repo-discovery, ...) just isn't there for that developer. This bites mixed-OS client teams even when generation happened on the owner's Mac.
confirmed.recommendation: Either stop committing the mirror (add `.claude/skills/` to the generated product's .gitignore and let `pnpm skills:sync` — run from `prepare`/postinstall — materialize it per machine, with the junction/copy fallback from the previous finding), or drop the symlink mirror entirely and make .claude/skills real checked-in directories kept in sync by the script. If Windows stays unsupported, document that Windows teammates must use WSL2 with the repo inside the WSL filesystem (an NTFS-mounted clone still has the problem).
confirmed.original_title: Every generated product ends up with 11 committed symlinks under .claude/skills — a Windows clone checks them out as plain text files and all skills silently disappear
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Chain verified: copier.yml excludes .claude/skills from the copy but the skills:sync task (copier.yml:72) recreates the symlinks after git init, and neither the template's HEAD .gitignore nor the product's ignores .claude/skills, so the client commits them. Downgraded from high: native Windows is outside the template's stated macOS/Linux envelope, and for a non-WSL Windows dev the rest of the harness ($CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR hooks) is broken anyway — the silent skill loss is real for mixed-OS teams but not the marginal breakage.

confirmed.title: Hook and skill counts drift: .github/README says 15 hooks / 11 skills; repo has 17 registered hooks and 13 skills, and harness.md omits three hooks
confirmed.evidence: .github/README.md:106-109 "**15 hooks** … **11 skills**". .claude/hooks/ holds 17 hook scripts, all registered in .claude/settings.json (incl. comment-policy.mjs, contract-enum.mjs, kill-orphan-dev-servers.mjs — none listed in harness.md §Repo hooks); .agents/skills/ holds 13 skills (creating-issues and template-update missing from the .claude/skills symlink set, so counts differ by directory too).

confirmed.recommendation: Add comment-policy, contract-enum and kill-orphan-dev-servers entries to harness.md §Repo hooks; replace hard counts in .github/README.md with non-numeric phrasing or make the counts part of the release checklist; run pnpm skills:sync so .claude/skills matches .agents/skills.
confirmed.original_title: Hook and skill counts drift: .github/README says 15 hooks / 11 skills; repo has 17 registered hooks and 13 skills, and harness.md omits three hooks

confirmed.title: CI never runs the combined (no-args) catalog:check, the only configuration that has caught cross-entry defects
confirmed.evidence: catalog.yml:43 matrix `entry: [identity, attachment, audit, notification, tag]`; :80 `run: pnpm catalog:check ${{ matrix.entry }}` — no job runs `pnpm catalog:check` bare (all entries in one child). Lessons L-010 ('A per-entry catalog:check pass does not prove multi-entry compatibility — run the combined catalog:check … at least once before closing a catalog change that touches more than one entry', evidence CAT-03 exit 7) and L-013/L-023 (sibling attach silently skipped only in combined installs) record real failures only the combined run exposed.
confirmed.why: The template's own history shows two multi-entry-only defects; the standing CI gate structurally cannot catch the next one, so it will be found by a client's product instead.
confirmed.recommendation: Add one matrix row (or a sixth job) running `pnpm catalog:check` with no arguments — same services, ~minutes — so every PR exercises the all-entries child.
confirmed.original_title: CI never runs the combined (no-args) catalog:check, the only configuration that has caught cross-entry defects
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: No workflow, package script pipeline or hook runs bare `pnpm catalog:check` (only the per-entry matrix at catalog.yml:80), and the repo's own lessons ledger (.specs/LESSONS.md L-010, L-013/L-023) records real defects — exit 7, silently skipped sibling DDL attach — that only the combined all-entries install exposed. The standing gate structurally cannot catch the class of defect the template has already hit twice.

confirmed.title: feedback-triage.yml workflow shipped to every product depends on an endpoint, secret and doc that don't exist in a kernel-only product
confirmed.evidence: Workflow calls `"$API_BASE_URL/v1/internal/feedback-triage/$FEEDBACK_ID"` with `secrets.FEEDBACK_TRIAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN` and `secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, pins `--model claude-sonnet-5` (line 80); no `feedback` entry exists in catalog/ (attachment, audit, identity, notification, schema, tag) and the kernel exposes no such route; issue-tracker.md.jinja:48 references "operation in `../dev/triagem-de-feedback.md`" but docs/dev contains only deploy.md.jinja, local-environment.md, template-changelog.md, template.md — the link is broken in every product.
confirmed.why: Every client receives a pt-BR GitHub workflow wired to a feedback module that neither the kernel nor the catalog provides, referencing a nonexistent operations doc and a hardcoded model id. It's dead machinery at best (repository_dispatch never fires) and misleading harness surface at worst (issue-tracker doc describes `triagem-ia` issues that can never exist).

confirmed.original_title: feedback-triage.yml workflow shipped to every product depends on an endpoint, secret and doc that don't exist in a kernel-only product
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: feedback-triage.yml is absent from copier.yml's exclude list (grep 'feedback' in copier.yml matches nothing) so every product receives it: a pt-BR workflow calling $API_BASE_URL/v1/internal/feedback-triage/$FEEDBACK_ID (line 36) with secrets FEEDBACK_TRIAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN + CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (line 74) and pinned `--model claude-sonnet-5` (line 80), while the kernel has zero feedback code (grep across apps/api/src is empty) and no catalog entry provides it; issue-tracker.md.jinja:52 links ../dev/triagem-de-feedback.md, which does not exist in docs/dev. confirmed.title: Callback bearer token is sent to a URL taken verbatim from the repository_dispatch payload — a defense-in-depth gap exploitable only by a holder of a dispatch-capable (repo-write) credential, notably enabling dev-backend compromise to exfiltrate the repo-level prod callback token
confirmed.evidence: L26 `API_BASE_URL: ${{ github.event.client_payload.apiBaseUrl }}` then the secret is handed to that host verbatim: L35-37 `curl ... -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API_BASE_URL/v1/internal/feedback-triage/$FEEDBACK_ID"` (TOKEN=secrets.FEEDBACK_TRIAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN), and again L62-64 and L157-161 (the verdict POST). apiBaseUrl comes straight from client_payload with no allowlist/validation.
confirmed.why: repository_dispatch is fired by the product backend holding a write-capable PAT. If that PAT leaks (or any repo-write collaborator/insider fires a dispatch), a payload of `{apiBaseUrl:"https://attacker.tld"}` causes the long-lived internal-API bearer (FEEDBACK_TRIAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN) to be POSTed to the attacker's server on the first curl. It is a defense-in-depth failure that turns a single credential compromise into a second-credential exfiltration, and it ships identically to every client repo.
confirmed.recommendation: Do not derive the token's destination from untrusted event data. Store the API base URL as a repo variable/secret (e.g. vars.FEEDBACK_API_BASE_URL), or validate client_payload.apiBaseUrl against a configured allowlist of hosts before any curl that carries the Authorization header. If per-environment URLs are needed, map client_payload.environment -> a trusted URL via a lookup, never trust the URL itself.
confirmed.original_title: Callback bearer token is sent to an attacker-influenceable URL taken from the dispatch payload (token exfiltration / SSRF)
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Fact verified exactly (L26 API_BASE_URL from client_payload, bearer curled to it at L35-37, L62-64, L157-161, no validation). But firing repository_dispatch requires a contents:write credential, and in this repo that credential can already reach secrets another way (push triggers ci.yml, which executes repo code — pnpm install lifecycle — with secrets in scope), so the added escalation is real but incremental, not a standalone high. The concrete residual value: a fine-grained PAT held by the less-protected dev backend exfiltrates the shared repo-level token silently, without any push. Defense-in-depth gap → medium.

confirmed.title: allowedTools grants the whole `gh issue` verb family (edit/close/delete/transfer), widening prompt-injection blast radius
confirmed.evidence: L82 `--allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Bash(gh issue:*),Bash(gh search:*)"`. The `gh issue:*` glob authorizes not just `create`/`comment` but `gh issue edit`, `gh issue close`, `gh issue delete`, `gh issue transfer`. Feedback body/attachments (user-submitted via the product) reach the prompt as data (L92-94 guard), but the only hard boundary on a successful injection is this allowlist.
confirmed.why: The prompt-injection guard is advisory; the tool allowlist is the real containment. With `gh issue:*` an injection that defeats the guard can close or delete arbitrary issues in the client's repo, edit labels/titles, or transfer issues out — not merely create a spam issue. The verdict step also assumes at most one issue is created; broad `gh issue` access does not enforce that.
confirmed.recommendation: Narrow to the verbs triage actually needs: `Bash(gh issue create:*),Bash(gh issue comment:*),Bash(gh issue list:*),Bash(gh issue view:*)`. Drop edit/close/delete/transfer. This preserves the documented flow (read relato, search duplicate, publish, comment on duplicate) while removing destructive verbs from the injection surface.
confirmed.original_title: allowedTools grants the whole `gh issue` verb family (edit/close/delete/transfer), widening prompt-injection blast radius
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: L82 grants Bash(gh issue:*), covering edit/close/reopen/transfer beyond the create/comment/list/view the documented flow needs; the workflow's own permissions block grants issues:write (L15) so close/edit/reopen of arbitrary issues would succeed (delete needs admin and would fail). Unlike findings 1-2, the untrusted input here is genuinely unprivileged — any product end-user's feedback text/attachments reach the prompt — and the only hard boundary after the advisory 'this is DATA' guard (L92-94) is this allowlist. Real, reachable injection blast-radius widening; medium is right.

confirmed.title: Released tag v2.2.1 ships the platform-feedback docs (docs/dev/template.md 'Giving an improvement back' section, issue-tracker.md.jinja pointer) while the .gitignore entry, the skill files AND the `pnpm platform feedback` CLI command are all still uncommitted — a product cut from v2.2.1 gets a documented flow whose command does not exist and whose drafts are untracked
confirmed.evidence: The `.gitignore` hunk adding '# rascunhos do fluxo platform-feedback ... .platform-feedback/' is in `git diff HEAD` (uncommitted), while HEAD:docs/dev/template.md:156 already tells the product to 'draft `.platform-feedback/<slug>.md`'. The flow's own SKILL.md calls the directory '(gitignored)' and the validator writes `<slug>.issue.md` (with stamped versions and code evidence) next to the draft.
confirmed.why: If the docs half ships without the gitignore half (exactly the split HEAD has today), products following the documented flow accumulate draft files containing code snippets and version stamps as plain untracked files; an agent doing a broad `git add .` commits them into the product repo, contradicting the skill's own 'never versioned' contract.
confirmed.recommendation: Commit the `.gitignore` line in the same commit as the feedback docs/implementation (see finding 1); this is one more reason the feature must land atomically.
confirmed.original_title: At HEAD, docs instruct writing feedback drafts to `.platform-feedback/` but the gitignore entry for it is uncommitted — a product cut from HEAD leaves evidence-bearing drafts unignored
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Verified and worse than claimed: HEAD is tagged v2.2.1 (56a9276), git show HEAD:docs/dev/template.md documents drafting .platform-feedback/<slug>.md and running `pnpm platform feedback`, git show HEAD:.gitignore has no .platform-feedback entry (exit 1), and git status shows .gitignore/cli.mjs modified with .agents/skills/platform-feedback/ and lib/commands/feedback.mjs untracked — so the tag also lacks the command itself (v2.2.0 has zero platform-feedback mentions; the docs half landed inside v2.2.1). Consequence for a v2.2.1 child: the flow fails loudly at the CLI and any drafts an agent writes anyway sit unignored for a broad `git add .`. Fails loudly and the drafts land in the product's own private repo, so medium, not high; the fix is the atomic commit the finding already recommends.

confirmed.title: security-hardening-2 follow-ups (attach_audit hook enforcement, reverse install order) exist only as prose in .specs — no spec, no issue, no lint rule
confirmed.evidence: validation.md:177-186 'Residual notes … carried for the follow-up spec': 'Reverse install order untested — nothing executes PERFORM identity.attach_audit() at 04_audit_attach_hook.sql:52-56' and 'No enforcement of the hook contract — audit.attach_module_hooks() finds hooks by name, so a future auditable entry that forgets to declare <schema>.attach_audit() silently gets no trail: exactly the failure class wave 8 just fixed. A catalog:lint rule or a coverage test would prevent the regression.' STATE.md:40 (AD-032) records the same as 'Open follow-up (security-hardening-2)'. `rg 'security-hardening-2'` outside .specs returns nothing; .specs/features/ has no such folder; `grep attach_audit scripts/platform/catalog-lint.mjs scripts/platform/lib/*.mjs` returns nothing.
confirmed.why: The 'silently no audit trail in a fresh child' bug cost two Verifier rounds to find; the guard that prevents its recurrence for the NEXT entry is explicitly named and not implemented, and the follow-up has no artifact an agent or the owner would ever be prompted by.
confirmed.recommendation: Open the security-hardening-2 spec (or at least a GitHub issue), and implement the cheap half now: a catalog-lint rule that an entry whose module.json/README declares audited tables (or that ships tables at all and lists audit interop) must ship a migrations/custom/*attach_audit* declaring `<schema>.attach_audit()`; add a script-level test installing audit before identity to exercise the self-PERFORM path.
confirmed.original_title: security-hardening-2 follow-ups (attach_audit hook enforcement, reverse install order) exist only as prose in .specs — no spec, no issue, no lint rule
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: validation.md:177-181 carries both residual notes verbatim, STATE.md AD-032 repeats 'Open follow-up (security-hardening-2): nothing enforces that a new auditable entry declares the hook', .specs/features/ has no security-hardening-2 folder (only done/ and template-update-contract/), and attach_audit appears zero times in catalog-lint.mjs and lib/lint.mjs. This is acknowledged debt, but the class it leaves unguarded (a future auditable entry silently getting no audit trail) is the exact bug wave 8 cost two Verifier rounds, and no artifact outside .specs prose will ever prompt the work. Medium as stated.

confirmed.title: Entry version 2.0.0 names two different trees (v2.0.0 without the remediation, v2.1.0 with it — 121 files apart) and the ADV-20260822 affects ranges (>=1.0.0 <2.0.0) can never match a 2.0.0 lock — but no child can realistically hold a vulnerable 2.0.0 lock (v2.0.0 module add always failed with exit 8), so the residue is latent bookkeeping ambiguity, not a live silent-vulnerability channel
confirmed.evidence: `git show v2.0.0:catalog/identity/single-tenant/module.json` and `git show v2.1.0:...` both say '"version": "2.0.0"' (all five entries; same at v2.2.0/HEAD) while `git diff --stat v2.0.0 v2.1.0 -- catalog/identity` shows 121 files / 3321 insertions; `git merge-base --is-ancestor f1e76ca v2.0.0` exits 1 (the identity-2.0.0 remediation release is not in v2.0.0). All five ADV-20260822-0*.md carry `affects: ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0"`, and scripts/platform/lib/advisories.mjs:69 filters with `semver.satisfies(installed.version, advisory.affects)` — a lock at 2.0.0 never matches, so pending-advisories.mjs stays silent. Documented as open: STATE.md:40 (AD-032) 'entries stay 2.0.0 — … a proper entry bump is a follow-up', and tasks.md closeout (commit a0f82a4): 'Known residue: … a child that installed an entry from v2.0.0 must apply ADV-20260822-* by hand; a proper entry bump is a security-hardening-2 candidate.'
confirmed.why: AD-016 makes advisory `affects` target entry versions; with two different trees under one immutable version number, the advisory channel — the template's designed mechanism for reaching children with security fixes — cannot distinguish a vulnerable 2.0.0 from a remediated one. Blast radius today is narrow (issue #9 made module add from v2.0.0 fail, and the .copier-answers fixture bug pinned most children to the v1.0.0 catalog), but the ambiguity is permanent until the bump.
confirmed.recommendation: Cut the promised entry bump (e.g. 2.0.1 for all five, CHANGELOG heading + advisory noting it is content-identical to the remediated 2.0.0), and widen/duplicate the ADV-20260822 affects so a pre-remediation 2.0.0 lock is caught (e.g. ">=1.0.0 <2.0.1" once bumped). Consider a catalog-lint rule: an advisory whose `fix` targets version X must have `affects` excluding X but including the previously released version.
confirmed.original_title: Entry-version residue: the same entry version 2.0.0 exists at v2.0.0 (without the security remediation) and v2.1.0 (with it), and the ADV-20260822 advisories' affects range cannot match it — promised entry bump still not done
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Every fact verified: identity single-tenant module.json says version 2.0.0 at both v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 (kernelRange differs), git diff shows 121 files/3321 insertions between them, f1e76ca is not an ancestor of v2.0.0, all five ADV-20260822 advisories carry affects '>=1.0.0 <2.0.0', and advisories.mjs:69 filters by semver.satisfies. But AD-033 records that v2.0.0's entries were uninstallable (kernelRange excluded kernel 2.0.0, exit 8 on any module add), so the only path to an un-remediated 2.0.0 lock is a manual port-module-update from exactly the v2.0.0 tag — narrow and speculative; children on 1.x are correctly caught by the existing affects range, and installs from v2.1.0+ get the remediated tree needing no advisory. Real, documented, permanent residue that should be closed with the promised bump, but the concrete silent-miss scenario is nearly unreachable → medium, not high.

confirmed.title: check-journal's decisive against-base check is hardwired to origin/main and silently downgrades to a warning when that ref is absent
