confirmed.title: No gate detects a missing/lost meta snapshot; drizzle-kit then silently regenerates already-applied tables into the next migration
confirmed.evidence: Empirical probe on an exact copy of apps/api with the pinned drizzle-kit 0.31.10: after generating a correct 0002_product_first.sql, deleting meta/0002_snapshot.json → `drizzle-kit check` prints "Everything's fine 🐶🔥" (exit 0) and the next `drizzle-kit generate` re-emits `CREATE TABLE "invoices"` into 0003_after_lost_snapshot.sql — a duplicate CREATE that crashes db:migrate in every environment that already ran 0002. check-journal.ts passes too: checkFilePairing() only pairs `${entry.tag}.sql` files ("if (!existsSync(join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, `${entry.tag}.sql`)))") and checkWhenOrdering() orders `when`s — the file never reads meta/ snapshots.
confirmed.why: check-journal exists precisely because a silent migration-skip "travou a homologação em 2026-07" (its own header comment), yet the symmetric silent failure — snapshot loss via a bad merge-conflict resolution or manual cleanup of the 50KB+ meta JSONs — passes every gate (drizzle-kit check, check-journal pre-push, CI tests) and corrupts the client's next migration. In a multi-client template this will eventually bite a real product, and the resulting duplicate-DDL migration bricks boot of already-migrated environments.
confirmed.recommendation: Extend check-journal.ts with a snapshot-pairing check: every journal entry idx must have meta/<idx padded>_snapshot.json (allowlist the shipped 0001 until the finding below is fixed). It is a pure fs check — offline-safe, portable, no false positives. Optionally also assert the prevId chain of the snapshots is unbroken.
confirmed.original_title: No gate detects a missing/lost meta snapshot; drizzle-kit then silently regenerates already-applied tables into the next migration
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified in code: checkFilePairing() pairs only `${entry.tag}.sql` and checkWhenOrdering() orders `when`s — no code in check-journal.ts or elsewhere reads meta/ snapshots. Combined with the probe's empirical demonstration that drizzle-kit check passes and generate re-emits already-applied DDL after snapshot loss, the silent-corruption path exists and the proposed fs-only gate is the right shape.

confirmed.title: At-rest outbox redaction matches the substring 'link' (and 'token', etc.) against arbitrary product payload keys, corrupting archived and dead-lettered events that replay
confirmed.evidence: outbox.dispatcher.ts:293 dead-letter `payload: redactSensitive(row.payload).value` and markPublished rewrites payload when changed; sensitive-keys.ts:8 fragment list includes "link" with case-insensitive substring matching (isSensitiveKey). So product keys like `linkedUserId`, `permalink`, `blinkRate` become "[REDACTED]" in the stored envelope; outbox-replay.ts re-inserts that payload for redispatch. The over-match hazard was recognized for logs ('ip' made exact, log.redact.ts LOG_EXACT) but not for the data-at-rest path; the design doc only accepts losing genuinely secret fields (design.md:242).
confirmed.why: For any client whose domain vocabulary contains 'link'/'token' as an innocent substring, replayed events (the operational recovery path the CLI exists for) silently deliver "[REDACTED]" where real identifiers were — data corruption that surfaces long after the write.
confirmed.recommendation: For the outbox at-rest path, match sensitive keys exactly (or word-boundary) rather than by substring — e.g. an exact-set {password, token, secret, authorization, cookie, link} plus explicit variants — keeping substring matching only for logs where false positives are cheap.
confirmed.original_title: At-rest outbox redaction matches the substring 'link' (and 'token', etc.) against arbitrary product payload keys, corrupting archived and dead-lettered events that replay

Innocent keys like linkedUserId/permalink match. The exact-match treatment given to 'ip' in log.redact.ts (LOG_EXACT) confirms the over-match hazard was known but not applied to the at-rest path.

confirmed.title: nginx: index.html served with no cache-control (stale-deploy white screens) and /assets/ location silently drops the security headers by declaring its own add_header
confirmed.evidence: nginx.conf:30-33 `location /assets/ { expires 1y; add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable"; }` — an add_header in a location cancels inheritance of the server-level X-Content-Type-Options/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy (the .mjs block at :42-49 even documents this rule and repeats them; /assets/ does not). No `location = /index.html` with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so browsers heuristically cache index.html and can reference purged hashed bundles after a deploy.
confirmed.why: Every product inherits a classic SPA failure mode: after any deploy, returning visitors can load a cached index.html pointing at assets that no longer exist → blank page until hard refresh. And hashed JS/CSS — the bulk of responses — are served without nosniff, inconsistent with the file's own stated intent (defense-in-depth headers 'always').
confirmed.recommendation: Add `location = /index.html { add_header Cache-Control "no-cache"; ...repeat security headers...; }` (and make the catch-all `/` no-cache too), and repeat the three security headers inside `location /assets/` exactly as the .mjs block already does.
confirmed.original_title: nginx: index.html served with no cache-control (stale-deploy white screens) and /assets/ location silently drops the security headers by declaring its own add_header
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: nginx.conf:30-33 verified: location /assets/ declares its own add_header Cache-Control, which per nginx inheritance rules (explicitly acknowledged in the file's own .mjs-block comment, 'add_header também não herda quando o nível de baixo declara os seus') drops nosniff/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy for all hashed assets; the .mjs regex block repeats them, /assets/ does not. No location = /index.html with no-cache exists, so heuristic caching of index.html after deploys is a real stale-bundle failure mode every product inherits. Medium.

confirmed.title: localStorage access is unguarded in code that runs on every navigation — throws in storage-blocked browsers (Safari private mode quota, Chrome 'block all cookies')

confirmed.why: In browsers where storage is blocked (Chrome/Edge with cookies blocked throw SecurityError on any localStorage access; older Safari private mode throws QuotaExceededError on setItem) every navigation throws inside the router subscriber, and logout broadcast throws mid-logout. confirmed.title: parseArgs treats every `--flag` as value-taking: a boolean flag before the entry name swallows it and surfaces as a bogus 'catálogo inacessível' error
confirmed.evidence: cli.mjs:27-31: any `--key` followed by a non-dash token consumes it as its value. Reproduced: `module add --force epsilon --catalog-ref <cat>` -> options.force='epsilon', name=undefined -> stderr `catálogo inacessível ou módulo ausente: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received undefined`, exit 3. Same for --with-deps, --dry-run, --rollback, --skip-tests, --no-web-react, --keep placed before the positional.
confirmed.why: docs list the flags after the entry, but agents and humans routinely reorder flags; the failure is a misleading 'catalog unreachable' (exit 3) rather than a usage error, sending debugging in the wrong direction — bad for a harness that must have no false signals.
confirmed.recommendation: Declare boolean flags explicitly (a Set of known boolean option names) so they never consume the next token — or switch to util.parseArgs from node:util with a proper option spec; return USAGE_ERROR with the unknown/missing-name message.
confirmed.original_title: parseArgs treats every `--flag` as value-taking: a boolean flag before the entry name swallows it and surfaces as a bogus 'catálogo inacessível' error

Affects every boolean flag placed before the positional.

confirmed.original_title: resolveInstallOrder root order is still a readdir/LIFO artifact — the follow-up opened by vitest-migration F6 is unimplemented

confirmed.title: No gate ever measures a catalog entry against the 90 % coverage floor the product's pre-push hook enforces on installed module code
confirmed.evidence:
`scripts/platform/lib/child.mjs:76` `runGates` runs only `["check", "test", "test:db"]` on the rendered child; `pnpm test:coverage` appears nowhere in `scripts/` (grep for "coverage" in `scripts/` matches only `gates.test.mjs` assertions and `feedback.mjs`).
But the floor applies to installed module code: `vitest.coverage.mts:19` `include: ["apps/api/src/**/*.ts", …]` and entries install into `apps/api/src/modules/<name>` (`scripts/platform/lib/child-layout.mjs` `moduleDir`), with `apps/api/src/**` held to statements/branches/functions/lines ≥ 90 (`vitest.coverage.mts:56-66`).
Entry test density varies widely: `catalog/tag` has 37 production files under `api/` against 4 `.spec.ts` + 1 `.int-spec.ts` + 1 `.e2e-spec.ts`; `catalog/audit` 25 production files / 6+6+2 tests.
confirmed.why: A client runs `pnpm platform module add tag`, then their very next `git push` is blocked by a coverage floor the platform never validated for that entry — and the documented remedy ("never lower the floor, cover the code") pushes the cost onto the client for code they did not write.
confirmed.recommendation: Add `pnpm test:coverage` (or a scoped `--coverage.include=apps/api/src/modules/<entry>/**` run with the same thresholds) as the last step of `catalog:check` so an entry cannot be tagged below the floor the child enforces; alternatively document a per-module floor exemption and encode it in `vitest.coverage.mts`.
confirmed.original_title: No gate ever measures a catalog entry against the 90 % coverage floor the product's pre-push hook enforces on installed module code
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: runGates = ['check','test','test:db'] only (child.mjs:74-80), no coverage run anywhere in scripts/; vitest.coverage.mts includes apps/api/src/**/*.ts with a flat 90 floor per glob (thresholds block), entries install into apps/api/src/modules/<name>, and the child ships both the lefthook pre-push coverage step and the ci.yml test-coverage job (the copier _tasks prune deletes only catalog:* scripts, not test:coverage). Whether an entry actually breaches 90 is unproven (would need a full install+coverage run), so the verified fact is the missing gate, not a demonstrated red CI — medium.

confirmed.title: Non-atomic install: a failure during copyFiles leaves copied files on disk with no lock entry, so `--rollback` says 'nada para reverter'; `--with-deps` has no multi-module rollback
confirmed.evidence: The try block copies files then persists the lock per plan (`for (const plan of plans) { copyFiles(plan.files); ... lock = persistEntry(...) }`); only MigrationFailureError is caught — any fs error (EACCES, disk full) mid-copy escapes as a raw stack with files partially written and no lock entry, and runRollback for that name prints 'nada para reverter: <name> não está no lock'. With `--with-deps`, later failures leave deps installed; `--rollback` takes a single name and reverts only it (runRollback, add.mjs:58-82) — no way to unwind the chain except one-by-one in reverse order the user must infer.
confirmed.why: The advertised recovery story ('arquivos mantidos, use --rollback') only holds for failures after the lock write; the earliest failures are the ones that strand a half-copied module invisible to the tooling. TEMPLATE_ONLY_FILES deletion before the gates is documented as irreversible (apply.mjs:12-16), so that part is fine.
confirmed.recommendation: Write the lock entry (files list, migrations []) BEFORE copying, or wrap copyFiles in a catch that records the partial file list to the lock before rethrowing; document/implement `--rollback` over the whole `--with-deps` plan (reverse order).
confirmed.original_title: Non-atomic install: a failure during copyFiles leaves copied files on disk with no lock entry, so `--rollback` says 'nada para reverter'; `--with-deps` has no multi-module rollback
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified at HEAD: in add.mjs:185-207 each plan's copyFiles runs before its persistEntry and the catch handles only MigrationFailureError, so a fs error mid-copy strands partially written files with no lock entry ('nada para reverter', add.mjs:61-64); runRollback takes a single name so a failed --with-deps chain has no batch unwind. TEMPLATE_ONLY_FILES irreversibility is indeed documented as deliberate (apply.mjs:13-16), which the finding correctly excludes.

confirmed.title: `module adopt` crashes with a raw ENOENT stack when the vendored files are not at the expected paths — its exact target scenario
confirmed.evidence: adoptCommand passes planCopy's target paths to persistEntry; apply.mjs:144 sha256File(readFileSync) throws. Reproduced: `module adopt beta` in a child without beta's files -> uncaught `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../apps/api/src/modules/beta/beta.module.ts'` with full stack, non-CLI exit. Adopt exists precisely for modules 'the product already had before the catalog existed' (docs/dev/template.md:73) — hand-vendored code frequently lives at other paths or is partial.
confirmed.why: The v0.2 migration path (the documented reason adopt exists) crashes on any layout drift instead of reporting which expected files are missing; the process may also die after readLock but the operator gets no exit-code contract.
confirmed.recommendation: In adopt, hash only files that exist and report the missing ones (warn or require --force); never let ENOENT escape as a raw stack — map to a CLI error and a defined exit code.
confirmed.original_title: `module adopt` crashes with a raw ENOENT stack when the vendored files are not at the expected paths — its exact target scenario
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: adopt.mjs:26-42 passes planCopy target paths to writeLock (apply.mjs), whose sha256File does readFileSync on each path with no try/catch in adopt, cli.mjs, or the top-level await — any vendored file not at the expected path escapes as a raw ENOENT stack with a non-CLI exit code, in the exact scenario (pre-catalog hand-vendored code) adopt exists for.

confirmed.title: Batched `module add --with-deps` still copies all modules' files before any migration generation, so the first module's baseline absorbs every dependency's tables and the lock misattributes migrations — the journal-naming corruption itself was fixed at HEAD (commit 90f1d0d, closes #11)
confirmed.evidence: In the fresh child (lint.mjs patched in): `pnpm platform module add tag` -> "dependências ausentes (use --with-deps)" (exit 5); `... --with-deps` -> exit 9: "falha ao gerar migrações (journal) ... [migrations] 2 problema(s) no journal: 0004_identity_auth_events_append_only.sql: não está no journal — nunca vai rodar / 0005_identity_audit_attach_hook.sql: não está no journal". Resulting dir: journaled 0003/0004 are 53-byte drizzle stubs ("-- Custom SQL migration file, put your code below! --") and the real shipped SQL sits in unjournaled 0004/0005 (two different files both named 0004_*). Cause observed: add.mjs:187 copies ALL planned modules' files before add.mjs:200 generates per module, so 0002_notification_baseline.sql swallowed 18 CREATE TABLEs from all three modules (notification+identity+tag); identity's own baseline then generates nothing, and migrations.mjs:74 (`paddedIndex(startIdx + 1 + i)`) assumes the baseline consumed index startIdx, misnaming the file that should overwrite drizzle's custom stub. Meanwhile `pnpm catalog:check tag` in the template PASSES (exit 0, "catalog:check — OK: notification, identity/single-tenant, tag") because catalog-check.mjs:191 installs entries one `module add` at a time.
confirmed.why: The only path a real client has to install a module with dependencies — the one the CLI itself tells you to use — deterministically fails and leaves a corrupted migrations dir, while the template's own CI gate stays green because it exercises a different (sequential) code path.
confirmed.recommendation: Either generate migrations per module interleaved with that module's copy (mirroring catalog:check's sequential behavior), or derive the custom-migration file index from the journal AFTER each drizzle-kit invocation instead of assuming baseline+1+i. Add a catalog:check mode that runs one batched `module add <leaf> --with-deps` in a fresh child.

confirmed.title: All 24 hook/statusline commands use POSIX $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR expansion, which cmd.exe on native Windows would not expand — moot within the template's stated macOS/Linux support, but the relative-path form is free

On native Windows, Claude Code executes hook command strings via cmd.exe, which does not expand `$VAR` — node receives the literal path `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/...` and exits with 'Cannot find module'.
confirmed.why: Every SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit hook fails on every tool call: the advisory and template-behind context never injects, and all gates (docs-stay-lean, comment-policy, delegate-to-subagent, branch-only-in-worktree, ...) become error noise instead of gates. confirmed.recommendation: Hooks run with cwd = the project directory, so the env var is unnecessary: use the portable relative form `node .claude/hooks/<name>.mjs` (and `node .claude/statusline.mjs`) everywhere. That is a one-file mechanical change with zero cost on macOS/Linux.

confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Fact confirmed: settings.json contains 24 `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/..."` commands. But the audit's stated portability target is macOS/Linux, and the finding itself concedes native Windows is already unreachable via its sibling findings — so this is future-proofing polish, not a gap a supported client hits.

confirmed.title: client_payload.environment is interpolated into the agent prompt via ${{ }} instead of being delivered as data — prompt-injection surface, but only reachable by the same repo-write-privileged sender as the dispatch itself
confirmed.evidence: L91 `O ambiente de origem é "${{ github.event.client_payload.environment }}".` — this `${{ }}` value is spliced into the YAML `prompt:` block. Contrast with the run: steps, which correctly route payload fields through env (L25 FEEDBACK_ID, L26 API_BASE_URL) and reference `$FEEDBACK_ID` inside double quotes.
confirmed.why: GitHub's own guidance is to never interpolate `github.event.*` into an executed body; route it through env. Here a payload sender can put newlines/quotes/instructions in `environment` to break out of the intended sentence and inject prompt directives into an agent that holds CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and `gh issue`/`gh search` tools. The run: blocks were hardened this way; the prompt block was not.
confirmed.recommendation: Pass environment via `env:` (e.g. `TRIAGE_ENV`) and reference it from a file the agent reads, or inject it the same way relato.json is delivered (as data on disk), not through `${{ }}` interpolation into the prompt string. Keep the existing 'this is DATA not instructions' guard as a second layer.
confirmed.original_title: Untrusted client_payload.environment is string-interpolated directly into the Claude prompt instead of passed via env
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Fact verified (L90-91 splices the expression into the action's prompt input; run: steps route payload through env at L25-26). However this is an action input, not a shell body, so there is no script/YAML injection — only prompt injection — and the only party who controls the field is the backend holding the dispatch PAT, the same precondition as finding 1 with strictly less payoff. Dominated by finding 1; hardening is cheap and worth doing, but severity is low.

confirmed.title: Callback token is a long-lived static bearer reused on every run, not scoped or single-use

At minimum document the token's scope/rotation and confirm the endpoint is not reachable from the public internet.

confirmed.title: feedbackId/FEEDBACK_ID from the payload is concatenated unvalidated into internal-API URL paths

confirmed.title: Shipped journal records 0001_kernel_outbox_notify with no meta/0001_snapshot.json — a state drizzle-kit itself never produces, baked into every client repo
confirmed.evidence: meta/ contains only 0000_snapshot.json while _journal.json has entries idx 0 and 1. drizzle-kit 0.31.10's own `generate --custom` (the path scripts/platform/lib/migrations.mjs uses) DOES write a snapshot per custom entry — proven by the rendered demo child (runtime-probe scratchpad) where custom entries 0003/0004 each have a 57.4K snapshot copy; only 0001 has none. Probe confirms the hole is currently harmless: `drizzle-kit check` passes, the first product migration is minimal and correct (only the new table; NOTIFY objects never re-emitted since they exist only in SQL), numbering comes from the journal (next idx = 2), and 0002_snapshot.prevId links to 0000's id, silently skipping 0001.
confirmed.why: The template relies on undocumented drizzle-kit tolerance of a journal-idx > snapshot-idx gap (verified only for the pinned ^0.31.10 line), replicates a non-native meta state into every client's repo forever, and makes the clean invariant "one snapshot per journal entry" — the natural fix for the snapshot-loss gap above — impossible without a permanent allowlist.
confirmed.recommendation: Recreate 0001 the native way: from the 0000-only state run `pnpm --filter api exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name kernel_outbox_notify`, paste the existing trigger SQL into the generated file, and commit the resulting meta/0001_snapshot.json (copy of 0000 with a fresh id/prevId chain). Then the snapshot-pairing gate needs no allowlist. Tag as a template release so existing children pick it up via copier update.

confirmed.title: redis-rate-limiter.int-spec starts a private Redis container per run and its sliding-window assertion (1 s sleep inside a 2 s window) has ~1 s slack under CI contention; the 1100 ms/1 s-window assertion is safe
confirmed.evidence:
`redis-rate-limiter.int-spec.ts:17-21` starts its own `GenericContainer("redis:7-alpine")` in `beforeAll` even though `apps/api/test/setup/global-setup.ts` already starts one Redis per run and publishes it via `provide`/`inject` (`int-env.ts` even re-calls `ensureDockerRuntimeEnv()` "porque as suítes de Redis sobem container próprio dentro do worker").
Timing assertions: `:90` `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1000))` then expects the sliding window (2 s) to still deny; `:102` `setTimeout(r, 1100)` then expects a 1 s window to have expired.
confirmed.why: Both are classic flake sources under CI contention (a 100 ms margin on a 1 s window, and container startup cost paid twice per run). The e2e/int tiers already run four workers in parallel plus a second container start, so a slow runner can push the sleep past the window boundary and fail the coverage gate for a reason unrelated to the code — the same class of failure already observed in application-pool.int-spec.
confirmed.recommendation: Consume the run's Redis through `containerRedisUri()`/`flushRedis()` like the rest of the tier instead of starting a private container, and make the window assertions robust (use `vi.useFakeTimers` where the limiter allows an injected clock, or widen the margins to ≥2× the window slack).
confirmed.original_title: redis-rate-limiter.int-spec starts a second Redis container inside a worker and asserts on 1 s / 1.1 s wall-clock sleeps against a 2 s window
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: Private GenericContainer confirmed (spec:17) despite global-setup providing a shared redisUri — though the beforeEach flushall makes the isolation plausibly deliberate. The claimed '100 ms margin' is a misreading: the 1100 ms sleep asserts a 1 s window has expired, where extra delay only helps; only the 2-consumes-then-1 s-sleep sliding-window test can flake, and it needs ~1 s of overhead against a local container — an order of magnitude more slack than the application-pool flake actually observed. Real but minor: extra container startup cost plus one contention-sensitive assertion.

confirmed.title: Idempotency snapshot records any non-HttpException error (including 4xx DomainErrors) as status 500 / 'failed', so deterministic business failures are re-executed instead of replayed
confirmed.evidence: idempotency.interceptor.ts:183-187 `const status = err instanceof HttpException ? err.getStatus() : 500` — DomainError (the kernel's canonical error type, e.g. 409/422 subclasses with `status` field) is not an HttpException, so persistedStatus=500 → row marked 'failed' with body null; every retry with the same key wins reopen() and re-runs the handler rather than replaying the 4xx problem-details the first caller received.
confirmed.why: Replay semantics silently differ between HttpException-based and DomainError-based 4xx: the latter never replays, re-executing handlers on each retry and storing a wrong response_status in the audit row. Safe but inconsistent, and any DomainError with side-effect-free 4xx semantics loses the dedupe guarantee the decorator advertises.
confirmed.recommendation: Teach the interceptor about DomainError: `const status = err instanceof HttpException ? err.getStatus() : err instanceof DomainError ? err.status : 500`, persisting 4xx DomainErrors as 'completed' with their problem-details body (via the same toProblem mapping) so replay matches the filter's output.
confirmed.original_title: Idempotency snapshot records any non-HttpException error (including 4xx DomainErrors) as status 500 / 'failed', so deterministic business failures are re-executed instead of replayed
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: idempotency.interceptor.ts:183-188 computes status via `err instanceof HttpException` only; DomainError (kernel/errors/domain.error.ts) extends Error, not HttpException, and the interceptor never imports it. So a 4xx DomainError persists as status 500 / 'failed' with null body; repository.reopen (failed→in_progress CAS) then re-executes the handler on retry instead of replaying — dedupe guarantee and stored response_status are wrong for the kernel's own canonical error type. No safety issue (re-execution of a deterministic 4xx), so low is right.

confirmed.title: Kernel-tier tests skip @Idempotent/@UseCase/IdempotencyCleanup — but @Idempotent is exercised end-to-end by catalog/identity's idempotency.e2e-spec.ts in template CI, and @UseCase metadata is write-only (inert); the genuine untested surface is small

Coverage run (`pnpm test:coverage`, 722 tests, all green): `....decorator.ts | 50 | 100 | 0 | 50 | 20` for `idempotent.decorator.ts`, `...cy.cleanup.ts | 50 | 100 | 50 | 50 | 22-23` for `idempotency.cleanup.ts`, and `kernel/use-case ....decorator.ts | 0 | 100 | 0 | 0 | 3-7`.

But the 'wrong metadata key would break with no red test' consequence is overstated: catalog/identity/api/__e2e__/idempotency.e2e-spec.ts drives replay through real @Idempotent controllers and runs in the template's catalog:check CI, so a decorator regression goes red there; USE_CASE_METADATA has zero readers anywhere (grep), so only Injectable matters and DI failures surface in every catalog test. confirmed.title: @swc/core is missing from pnpm-workspace.yaml's already-explicit built-dependencies lists, so every install prints the 'Ignored build scripts' warning

Run \"pnpm approve-builds\" to pick which dependencies should be allowed to run scripts." (everything still builds and all tests pass, so the native binding is not required).

confirmed.title: `rm -rf` in shipped package.json clean scripts fails under cmd.exe
confirmed.evidence: package.json:33 `"clean": "turbo clean && rm -rf node_modules"` (kept by the copier prune task — only catalog:* / template:smoke / test:scripts are deleted, copier.yml:64); packages/api-client/package.json:37 `"clean": "rm -rf dist generated/.kubb"`.

confirmed.recommendation: Replace with a portable deletion: `node -e "fs.rmSync('node_modules',{recursive:true,force:true})"` or a devDependency like rimraf, in both files.

confirmed.title: zod is a devDependency of @platform/api-client although its generated runtime code imports zod/v4 at runtime
confirmed.evidence: packages/api-client/package.json puts `"zod": "^4.4.3"` under devDependencies (line 55) while @tanstack/react-query and axios — the other runtime imports of generated/src code — are under dependencies (lines 42-45). generated/zod/livenessSchema.ts:8 has a runtime `import { z } from "zod/v4"`, and the package's exports map serves that file both as workspace source (development condition) and as built dist (./dist/generated/zod/*.js).
confirmed.why: It works today only because pnpm installs devDependencies of all workspace packages. Under a production-pruned install, a future decision to publish/consume the package outside the workspace, or stricter dependency linting, the dist build's `zod/v4` import would be unresolvable; it also lets the web and api-client zod ranges drift independently with no declared relationship, which is the one scenario that could split the module instance (mitigated but not eliminated by the globalThis config).
confirmed.recommendation: Move zod from devDependencies to dependencies (or peerDependencies matching apps/web's range) in packages/api-client/package.json so the runtime import is declared and the version stays coupled to the consumer's.
confirmed.original_title: zod is a devDependency of @platform/api-client although its generated runtime code imports zod/v4 at runtime
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: packages/api-client/package.json declares zod ^4.4.3 under devDependencies while generated/zod/*.ts has runtime `import { z } from "zod/v4"` served through the exports map both as source and dist; apps/web declares its own zod ^4.4.3. Works today only via workspace dev installs; a pruned/production install or published package would fail to resolve, and the ranges can drift independently. Real but latent — low.

confirmed.title: serializeParams stringifies nested objects to "[object Object]" — object-shaped query params become silently broken filters
confirmed.evidence: client.ts:44-49: `if (Array.isArray(value)) { for (const item of value) search.append(key, String(item)) } else { search.append(key, String(value)) }` — a Date, object or array-of-objects param serializes as "[object Object]"/toString output with no error.
confirmed.why: The kernel's listing endpoints use flat params today, but the transport is the platform seam every product's entities go through; the first product that passes `{ filter: { status: "x" } }` or a Date gets a silently empty result set (the same silent-no-op class the comment above the function warns about for arrays).
confirmed.recommendation: Throw (or console.warn in dev) on non-primitive param values, or explicitly serialize Date to ISO and reject plain objects with a clear error naming the offending key.
confirmed.original_title: serializeParams stringifies nested objects to "[object Object]" — object-shaped query params become silently broken filters
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: client.ts:41-50 does String(value)/String(item) on everything non-null: a plain object or array of objects serializes to "[object Object]" with no error, the exact silent-no-op class the function's own comment guards against for arrays. Kernel endpoints use flat params today, so low.

confirmed.title: One malformed advisory file silently disables all advisory surfacing in the product
confirmed.evidence: loadAdvisories maps every ADV-*.md through parseAdvisory, which throws AdvisoryParseError; the hook's outer catch (pending-advisories.mjs: 'any failure exits silently') swallows it, so no pending advisory is ever shown again

confirmed.recommendation: Per-file try/catch in loadAdvisories, skipping the bad file and surfacing one line naming it.
confirmed.original_title: One malformed advisory file silently disables all advisory surfacing in the product
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: advisories.mjs:15-26 maps every ADV-*.md through parseAdvisory, which throws AdvisoryParseError on any malformed frontmatter (frontmatter.mjs:20-44); pending-advisories.mjs wraps everything in a catch that exits silently by design, so one bad file mutes all session-start advisory surfacing with no signal. Mitigated slightly by the CLI paths (status) failing loudly on the same file, so low as reported.

confirmed.title: Lock file diff noise: module map ordering is insertion-dependent and installedAt is a fresh timestamp on every reinstall
confirmed.evidence: writeLock spreads `{ ...lock.modules, [name]: ... }` — a rollback+reinstall moves the module to the end of the JSON object; entryBase sets `installedAt: new Date().toISOString()` (add.mjs:151).
confirmed.why: The lock is committed; churn in ordering/timestamps creates avoidable merge conflicts between teammates installing different modules — the same class of noise the template's own copier-conflict philosophy tries to eliminate.
confirmed.recommendation: Sort module keys on write (Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(...).sort())) and consider recording the catalog entry version-date instead of wall-clock, or keep installedAt only on first install.
confirmed.original_title: Lock file diff noise: module map ordering is insertion-dependent and installedAt is a fresh timestamp on every reinstall
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: apply.mjs:147 spreads `{...lock.modules, [name]: ...}` and rollback removes the key by destructuring (apply.mjs:165), so reinstall appends at the end; installedAt is a fresh timestamp on every install in both add.mjs:159 and adopt.mjs:37. Real but low-cost diff noise in a committed file.

confirmed.title: Was real, but already fixed at HEAD: e013a37 (v2.2.1, today) makes resolveCatalog reuse a valid immutable-ref cache and rm+reclone otherwise, with regression tests
confirmed.evidence: `const dest = path.join(cacheRoot, hashRef(resolvedRef));` then unconditional `git clone ... dest` with no existsSync/rm. Reproduced: two resolveCatalog calls with the same file:// source and cacheRoot → first `kind: git`, second `CatalogUnreachableError: ... fatal: destination path '.../cache/6409979c199b' already exists and is not an empty directory.` cacheRoot defaults to `tmpdir()/platform-catalog`, which persists between runs; catalog-source.test.mjs only ever uses a fresh `mkdtempSync` cacheRoot, so the collision is untested.
confirmed.why: For a git-sourced product (the normal case: `_src_path: gh:...`), the first `module add` works and every subsequent catalog command — installing a second module, `module list`, a retry after a failure — fails with a misleading 'catálogo inacessível' until the OS temp dir is wiped. That is a guaranteed second-day failure in every client product.
confirmed.recommendation: In resolveCatalog, if `dest` exists and looks valid (has `catalog/`), reuse it (the ref hash already keys the cache — for an immutable tag ref reuse is safe); otherwise `rmSync(dest, {recursive:true, force:true})` before cloning. Add a test that resolves the same git ref twice with a persistent cacheRoot.
confirmed.original_title: Second catalog resolution on the same machine fails: resolveCatalog clones into a cached dir it never checks or cleans
confirmed.verdict_reason: adjusted: The claim was accurate when filed, but catalog-source.mjs:98-108 now checks existsSync(dest), reuses a detached-HEAD (immutable-ref) clone via isReusableCache, and rmSync+reclones anything else; catalog-source.test.mjs:109-131 covers double resolution with a persistent cacheRoot ('issue #10'). Nothing left to do beyond what shipped in v2.2.1.

confirmed.title: `module add` never honors manifest `web.defaultRoot` (webRootFor always computes apps/web/src/entities/<name>), while `adopt` does — divergent semantics for the same manifest field
confirmed.evidence: add.mjs:142 `const webRoot = webRootFor(moduleName, options["web-root"])` is always defined, so plan.mjs:98's `webRoot ?? manifest.web?.defaultRoot` never falls through in add; adopt.mjs computes webRoot only when `--web-root` is passed, so it does use defaultRoot. catalog/identity/single-tenant/module.json:234 declares `"defaultRoot": "apps/web/src/entities/identity"` — only coincidentally equal to webRootFor('identity').
confirmed.why: A future catalog entry whose defaultRoot differs from the entities/<name> convention would install its web files to a different place via add vs adopt, and the schema (module.schema.json) advertises defaultRoot as meaningful.
confirmed.recommendation: In add, pass `options["web-root"] ? webRootFor(name, options["web-root"]) : undefined` (mirroring adopt) so planCopy's defaultRoot fallback applies, or drop defaultRoot from the schema and document the fixed convention.
confirmed.original_title: `module add` never honors manifest `web.defaultRoot` (webRootFor always computes apps/web/src/entities/<name>), while `adopt` does — divergent semantics for the same manifest field
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: Verified: add.mjs:142 always passes a defined webRoot (webRootFor defaults base to apps/web/src), so planCopy's `webRoot ?? manifest.web?.defaultRoot` (plan.mjs:98) never falls through in add, while adopt.mjs:25 passes undefined unless --web-root is given; catalog/schema/module.schema.json declares defaultRoot and identity's value only coincidentally matches the convention. Latent divergence, no current entry affected — low.

confirmed.title: `module list` requires catalog access and exits 3 offline even though everything it needs for the lock side is local
confirmed.evidence: listCommand: after printing nothing, `catalog = resolveCatalog(...)` and on error returns EXIT_CODES.CATALOG_UNREACHABLE without listing the installed modules from the lock (list.mjs:22-28).
confirmed.why: Offline or with the git-cache bug above, the user cannot even enumerate what is installed via the documented command (status partially compensates). 'Degrades gracefully offline' is an explicit template requirement.
confirmed.recommendation: Print the lock rows first with `catalog=?`, and only annotate HEAD versions when the catalog resolves; reserve exit 3 for when nothing at all can be shown.
confirmed.original_title: `module list` requires catalog access and exits 3 offline even though everything it needs for the lock side is local
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: list.mjs:21-27 returns CATALOG_UNREACHABLE (3) before printing any lock row when resolveCatalog throws, even though the lock is local; statusCommand (status.mjs formatModules) does list installed modules offline, which caps this at low as the finding itself acknowledges.

confirmed.title: `pnpm template:smoke` probes a fixed port 3222 and can pass against a developer's already-running API
confirmed.evidence: `scripts/template-smoke.mjs:18` `const HEALTH_PORT = "3222";` — the same value as the api's default `PORT` (`apps/api/src/shared/config/env.ts:14` `PORT: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(3222)`). `:218-235` spawns the child's `pnpm --filter api run start` with `PORT: HEALTH_PORT` and then `waitForHealth({ url: 'http://localhost:3222/health' })`.
confirmed.why: If the developer has `pnpm dev` running (the documented local loop), the child's server fails to bind while `waitForHealth` gets a 200 from the developer's own API — the smoke test passes without ever proving the generated product boots. The inverse (a busy port that answers nothing) fails the smoke for the wrong reason.
confirmed.recommendation: Bind an ephemeral port (0 / `getPort`) and read the chosen port from the child's stdout, or at minimum verify the responding process is the spawned child (probe a value only the child could return, e.g. its own `SERVICE_VERSION`) before declaring the check green.
confirmed.original_title: `pnpm template:smoke` probes a fixed port 3222 and can pass against a developer's already-running API
confirmed.verdict_reason: confirmed: template-smoke.mjs:18 hardcodes HEALTH_PORT=3222, identical to env.ts:14's API default, and waitForHealth probes localhost:3222 with no check that the responder is the spawned child — a developer's running `pnpm dev` yields a false pass. Scope is template-repo-only (copier.yml excludes scripts/template-smoke.mjs and deletes the script entry from the child package.json), so low.

confirmed.title: skills-lock.json carries a stale 'nestjs-expert' entry for a skill that is not vendored, and pins no source refs

refuted.title: kill-orphan-dev-servers can SIGTERM an unrelated vite process when lsof fails: empty cwd resolves to the session's own repo
refuted.reason: refuted: The claimed kill path is unreachable: kill-orphan-dev-servers.mjs:70-71 is `const repoRoot = repoRootOf(cwdOf(pid)); if (!repoRoot || gitCommonDir(repoRoot) !== sessionCommonDir) continue;` and repoRootOf("") can only return "" (existsSync('pnpm-workspace.yaml') relative hit → returns the empty `current`) or null (dirname("") is '.', loop exits) — both falsy, so `!repoRoot` short-circuits and the process is skipped before gitCommonDir("") is ever evaluated. An lsof failure therefore degrades to skip, not to kill.

refuted.title: .claude/settings.local.json with defaultMode bypassPermissions and owner-machine paths is committed to the template repo
refuted.reason: refuted: The central claim is factually wrong: `git ls-files` and `git ls-tree -r HEAD` show no .claude/settings.local.json, and `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '**/settings.local.json'` proves it was never committed in any ref. The file exists only untracked on the owner's disk, matched by the owner's global git ignore (~/.config/git/ignore), and copier.yml:32 excludes it from products — no contributor or client ever receives the bypassPermissions settings.

refuted.title: Right after `copier update`, the child's gates fail with a missing node module until a manual `pnpm install`
refuted.reason: refuted: The recommendation is already implemented: .agents/skills/template-update/SKILL.md step 2.4 explicitly runs `pnpm install`, then `pnpm skills:sync`, and only step 2.5 runs the gates — so 'the very first thing the skill does after copier update is run the gates' is factually wrong. The probe's stale-store observation came from running `pnpm check` directly after `copier update`, a sequence the skill does not prescribe, and the probe itself showed a plain `pnpm install` (the skill's mandated step) fixes it.

refuted.title: HEAD documents `pnpm platform feedback` + platform-feedback skill whose implementation exists only as uncommitted working-tree files — next tag ships dangling docs to every product

TRIGGER / ACCESS (known-debt Q1) — POSITIVE: the workflow triggers ONLY on `repository_dispatch: types:[feedback-triage]` (L6-8). repository_dispatch cannot be fired by an outside user's issue/comment, a fork, or an unauthenticated actor — it requires an API POST with a repo-write-capable token (the product backend's PAT). So the 'outside issue/comment reaches Claude' vector is NOT present. The residual untrusted input is the feedback CONTENT (any product end-user submits it), which reaches the agent as data on disk with a 'this is DATA not instructions' guard (L92-94); its blast radius is bounded by allowedTools (see findings #2/#3).

PERMISSIONS (Q3) — least-privilege is reasonable: `contents: read, issues: write, id-token: write` (L13-16); id-token:write is genuinely required by claude-code-action's OIDC exchange, issues:write is the minimum for the create/comment flow. GH_TOKEN passed to the action is github.token, repo-scoped. No over-broad `write-all`.

SHA PINNING / TOOLS (Q5) — GOOD: every action is SHA-pinned (checkout L28, claude-code-action L70 @24dcd50c…, catalog.yml/ci.yml likewise). allowedTools is constrained (no arbitrary Bash; the compound-command block and per-command permission model prevent `env`/`curl`/chaining — so env-var secret exfil via Bash is not reachable). show_full_output is deliberately OFF (L84-86) to keep user relato out of 90-day logs — sound. Callback token is kept in run: steps only, never in the agent env — sound, as the header comment claims.

catalog.yml / ci.yml — no script-injection: both use `pull_request` (NOT pull_request_target), so fork PRs run without secrets and with read-only token. The only event interpolation into a run: block is catalog.yml L35-36 (base.sha/head.sha), which are GitHub-generated 40-hex SHAs, not attacker-controlled strings — safe. ci.yml interpolates only github.ref into a concurrency group.
